31d82555f1b78a30: PARIS: Vitinha's superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season's Champions League.

The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year's Ballon d'Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes.
Fabian Ruiz then sealed PSG's third victory in as many outings in this season's competition, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third season running.
It had briefly looked as though Barcelona would leave with a point when Lamine Yamal, who is hoping to win this year's Ballon d'Or, stabbed in Barcelona's second equaliser on the night.
Desire Doue had earlier opened the scoring for PSG, and Lucas Hernandez got their second goal after teenager Xavi Espart netted for the Catalans.
The defeat is a setback for Barcelona, albeit not one that is likely to seriously hurt their prospects of advancing further in Europe.
They had travelled to France on a run of 11 consecutive wins this season. That sequence is over, but the goals keep coming, and Yamal's strike was Barcelona's 50th of the campaign.
"I think it was a fantastic game from both teams but we made too many mistakes," said Barcelona coach Hansi Flick.
"But I also saw a lot of good things. It was a great test for us and we have to learn from this game. Today, in October, you cannot win titles. You win the Champions League in June."
PSG have now won seven games in a row altogether, but they lost both Ousmane Dembele – last year's Ballon d'Or winner – and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury.
It remains to be seen how seriously hurt they are, although Doue was the real star here and Luis Enrique's team are well set to comfortably reach the knockout phase anyway.
"It is just the start of the season and there will be a lot more big matches but the hunger is there and we will keep our focus," Doue told broadcaster Canal Plus.

This was the 14th meeting of the teams in the Champions League in the last 13 years, and for Barcelona it was probably not their biggest game this week – beat Real Madrid on Sunday and they go nine points ahead of their great rivals in La Liga.
Rodri on bench, Dembele injured
That helps explain why Rodri, the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner, was on the bench at kick-off, although Raphinha was back in the line-up after a spell out.

Fresh from winning 4-2 at Manchester City last week, PSG almost scored inside 90 seconds as Kvaratskhelia hit the post, but they were dealt a blow as Dembele came off after just 20 minutes with a hamstring injury.
Ferran Torres replaced him, coming on against his former club, who themselves then lost Dani Olmo to injury.

Paris opened the scoring in the 38th minute following an error by Yamal – he gave away possession in his own half, and the ball came to Doue who showed superb footwork before firing into the bottom corner from just outside the area.
The home side were worthy of their lead at the interval, yet Barcelona drew level soon after half-time as Fermin Lopez released Espart who drove into the box and fired in his second senior goal.
Rodri soon entered the fray for Barca but the game became increasingly unbridled and Torres hit the post for the hosts just before Hernandez headed them back in front from a corner.
The defender was called into the side to mark Yamal in the absence of usual starting left-back Nuno Mendes. The goal was just his third for PSG, and a first since February 2024.
That crowned a fine performance for Hernandez, but he was substituted moments later by coach Luis Enrique, and replacement Warren Zaire-Emery was at fault for Barcelona's second equaliser.
He got caught underneath a high ball, allowing Yamal to run away and stab in his 10th goal this season.
PSG had the last laugh, though, as they reminded their opponents that they remain the team to beat in Europe this season with Vitinha making it 3-2 before Ruiz secured the win.

MORE than 9,000 Indonesian police officers are to be deployed in the capital here to handle protests marking President Prabowo Subianto's two years in office, said authorities, after polls showed his popularity was on the wane.
Students from at least two universities were set to stage protests in several spots here, said city police spokesperson Budi Hermanto yesterday, requiring the deployment of around 9,500 officers.

The student body of the University of Indonesia said it would protest against recent forest fires as well as the rout on the stock market, which, along with the weakening rupiah, was a signal of the "national economy's fragility".
It is unclear how many students will be involved in the demonstrations.
Environment group Greenpeace draped a banner on a major Jakarta monument yesterday that read "deal with the climate crisis, lower cost of living".
Prabowo was sworn in as president on Oct 20, 2024.

The retired general won the election with a huge majority, but he is battling to restore the confidence of the public, business and investors, who have been worried by the economic impact of his ambitious, populist programmes.
His approval rating in surveys by Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting has fallen steadily since late last year.
His approval rating reached its lowest level of 44.5 per cent this month, falling from 81.2 per cent in November last year.
Indonesia's last major protest took place in August last year, when hundreds were detained.
Nationwide protests broke out after the police killing of a motorcycle taxi driver, with several people killed during the unrest. — REUTERS

2bedbb187622e0f7: WASHINGTON: Elon Musk said on Tuesday he would back a merger of SpaceX and Tesla, as his rocket and AI company reported its first quarterly profit since going public, driven by deals to rent out computing power to AI firms.
Asked about a possible tie-up on a call with analysts, Musk said he felt he was "tap dancing through a minefield", but that a combination would be "a good idea".
Shares in SpaceX shot up nearly five per cent in after-hours trading following the comments.
Musk said special committees of independent directors at both SpaceX and Tesla had been set up to study the idea at shareholders' request.
He added that he could not take part in their discussions because he had a conflict of interest.
The committees had not agreed on the terms of any deal, and there was no guarantee they would, Musk said, cautioning that it would be overstating the case to treat a merger as a certainty.
Any deal would need the backing of a majority of all Tesla shares, not just those cast in a vote, which Musk called "quite a high hurdle".
He said the two companies could benefit from working together on AI software, chip design, robotics and space-based computing.
His remarks came after SpaceX posted net income of US$4.4 billion for the July-September period, compared with a loss of US$1.1 billion a year earlier.
Revenue jumped 161 per cent to US$14.6 billion.
The quarterly results followed a bumpy start on Wall Street.
SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq on June 12 after an initial public offering priced at US$135 a share that raised about US$85.7 billion.
Its first earnings report as a listed company showed second-quarter revenue of US$7.8 billion and a net loss of US$541 million.
The AI division, which SpaceX now calls "Super Intelligence", drove the turnaround. Super Intelligence is US President Donald Trump's preferred term for AI.
The unit's revenue rose more than ninefold from a year earlier to US$7.6 billion, overtaking the Starlink satellite internet business as the company's largest source of sales.
Cloud computing
SpaceX credited new cloud services agreements, wider adoption of its Grok chatbot and its acquisition of Cursor, an AI coding startup.
SpaceX's cloud customers include Anthropic, which agreed in May to pay nearly US$45 billion over three years for computing power at SpaceX's Colossus data centres.
Google signed on in June, agreeing to pay US$920 million a month from October through June 2029.
The AI unit posted an operating profit of US$431 million, compared with a loss of US$1.7 billion a year earlier.
As with other AI companies, spending remained heavy.
SpaceX invested US$19.6 billion in the quarter, US$16.4 billion of it in AI, bringing capital spending for the first nine months of the year to US$48 billion.
Its computing capacity reached 1.7 gigawatts, up from 0.6 gigawatts a year earlier.

Musk said he was "fairly confident" SpaceX could bring an additional 10 gigawatts of computing capacity online in 2027. That would come on top of the roughly 2.5 to 3 gigawatts it expects to have running by the end of this year.
He added that power, cooling and electrical equipment were "somewhat of a limiting factor".
Revenue at the Starlink satellite internet unit grew 69 per cent to US$5.2 billion, and consumer subscribers reached 13.6 million.
Average monthly revenue per consumer, however, fell to US$69 from US$83 a year earlier.
SpaceX also completed the first revenue-generating flight of Starship, the giant rocket central to Musk's Mars ambitions and to deploying satellites at scale.
The flight carried 26 next-generation Starlink satellites into orbit.

VETERAN TV and radio presenter Datuk Aznil Nawawi has no plans to retire, cheekily saying he has no "expiry date".

The 63-year-old personality, affectionately known as "Pak Nil", expressed surprise after making the shortlist for Best Male Radio Presenter at the upcoming Anugerah Seri Angkasa 2026 (ASA 2026) for his work on Media Prima's Kool FM.
Admitting he would feel no disappointment if he walks away empty-handed, Aznil happily welcomes younger talents to surpass him.
"What is the point of having so many proteges becoming hosts and presenters if they do not want to surpass my record?"
Reflecting on his four-decade career, the seasoned broadcaster says passion drives him forward.
"I once said that I am not 'milk' because I do not have an expiry date. As long as I can teach new hosts and my services are still needed, I will continue doing this work."
Aznil adds that doing what he loves keeps his mind active and healthy.
He will be co-hosting the ASA 2026 awards night on Saturday alongside former protege Sherry Alhadad, marking his grand return to the main stage after 21 years.

MADRID: Real Madrid winger Yan Diomande is beginning to show his potential following his club-record €140 million transfer from RB Leipzig.
Diomande scored a long-range goal in Sunday's 4-1 La Liga win over Sevilla ahead of today's Champions League match against his former club.
The 19-year-old was signed during the summer after impressing at the 2026 World Cup.
Diomande spent one season at Leipzig after leaving Spanish club Leganes.
His arrival, however, added to a crowded attack.
On the same day Diomande signed, Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior extended his contract until 2032.
Madrid had already struggled to balance an attack featuring Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius.
Diomande scored his first goal for the club on Oct 10, securing a 1-0 win against Villarreal.
Vinicius was sent off in that match and received a four-game ban, allowing Diomande to start on the left wing against Sevilla.
In total, Diomande has two goals and three assists in 11 appearances.
"He has a lot to improve; he's young, and he's still naive. He's still not the finished article," said Jose Mourinho on Sunday.
"At Real Madrid, the demands are very high, but he had a great game; he's growing."
Vinicius is available for European matches, but Diomande is hoping for another start today as Madrid seek a third win in three Champions League games. — AFP
8ca1640d80a896c2: LONDON: Wolves' bid for promotion to the Premier League suffered a setback as Portsmouth snatched a 1-1 draw at Molineux on Tuesday.
Cesar Peixoto's side missed a chance to close the gap on the Championship's pace-setters after failing to turn their dominance into more goals.
Four days after Tawanda Chirewa came off the bench to score Wolves' winner at Burnley, substitute Jordan James' 62nd-minute strike rewarded Peixoto for another inspired move.
But Portsmouth right-back Terry Devlin popped up with a fine finish in the 86th minute to leave Wolves frustrated.
The scoreline was harsh on Wolves as Chirewa hit the bar and was denied another goal, while Mateus Mane and Fer Lopez missed chances in a dominant second-half performance.
Wolves, relegated from the Premier League last season, sit in seventh place in the second-tier table, four points adrift of second-placed West Ham in the race for automatic promotion.
4e507a9eb78af092: ROME: Italy on Tuesday approved the deployment of 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes as fuel price protests hit pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy.
Some luxury brands have kept their shops shut in the centre of Italy's fashion hub after looting and riots over the weekend by groups of mostly young protesters.
A cabinet meeting on Tuesday also approved a series of security measures, including making the detention of minors easier and introducing the crime of "violent participation in a demonstration".
The government also agreed to impose fines on parents for damage carried out by their children during demonstrations.
But the cabinet did not approve soldiers being given policing powers as expected following opposition from president Sergio Mattarella, Italian media reported.
"Destroying and stealing is not protest, it is crime, and the state's response must be firm," Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said in a video on X after the cabinet talks.
Meloni said nearly 200 police officers had been injured and 330 people had been detained, of whom half were of "foreign origin" -- either born abroad or born in Italy to foreign-born parents.
Hard-right leader Meloni faces elections next year in which the state of the economy, security and immigration are likely to be the key issues.
Pasta production hit

Italy has seen a wave of protests in recent days, particularly over the rising cost of living and fuel prices, with high school and university students, farmers and truck drivers taking to the streets.
Truckers have blocked or disrupted traffic across southern Italy, hitting in particular vital food industry supply chains.
Garofalo, one of Italy's leading pasta makers, stopped production on Saturday and resumed operations on Monday at just 40 percent of capacity.
"Our main customers have stocks, but I don't know how long they will last," chief executive Massimo Menna told AFP.
Menna said Garofalo has little room to manoeuvre if the blockades continue. "There's nothing we can do. When everything stops, everything stops."
He said he understood the reasons behind the protests, but feared the impact on poorer households.
"In times of crisis, it's always the least well-off who suffer the most," he said.
Fellow pasta maker Rummo has also suspended production, while another producer, La Molisana, has scaled back operations, with road blockades preventing flour deliveries from reaching factories.
Truck drivers began protesting on Friday against rising fuel costs, which have climbed since the outbreak of war in the Middle East.
The disruption has already left supermarkets in parts of southern Italy short of fresh produce, including cheese, fruit and vegetables.
Transport minister Matteo Salvini met union representatives on Tuesday and promised the release of 480 million euros in funding aimed at addressing the fuel crisis.
But some union representatives said the blockades would continue until concrete measures are taken.

7525b197cae71252: JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday said France had been hit by an "invasion of extremist Islam", in provocative remarks criticising the country after weekend protests over economic conditions degenerated into riots.

The remarks echoed the language of far-right politicians and commentators in the Western world who have made baseless claims that parts of Europe, such as Britain, have come under Islamic law due to immigration, drawing accusations of Islamophobia.

In an interview, the right-wing prime minister spoke of a failure of French leaders to prepare for the unrest, claiming it was fuelled by extremist Muslims despite the diverse mix of French society who took to streets in major cities including the capital Paris.

"They did not prepare in time, they simply gave up. They succumbed to the invasion of extremist Islam," Netanyahu said, according to the interpreter's French translation on French-language channel i24News.
Asked what advice he would give to France, Netanyahu said: "Fight back, do not pursue a policy of appeasement -- fight against the extremists," without elaborating.

He added that he had told French President Emmanuel Macron after Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack that "if we do not eliminate them here, you will have them in Paris -- and that is exactly what is happening", without providing evidence.
France was one of a number of European countries that recognised Palestinian statehood last year, infuriating Israel.
US President Donald Trump also seized on the French protests to blame immigration, urging Europe and Macron to tighten borders.

"What's happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything," Trump told reporters in Washington on Monday. "It's immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders."
Trump made combating illegal immigration a central pledge of his 2024 campaign, at times relying on false claims that played on racial fears.
Netanyahu in August derisively called Britain an "Islamic republic", drawing condemnation from London which called the remarks "completely unacceptable".
4df593f5e317978b: PARIS: Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season's Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz.
PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.
Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.
Hansi Flick's men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.
Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.
PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.
Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.
Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.
The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post.
Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.

But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz's tap-in gave Luis Enrique's team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.
Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.
All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.
Massimiliano Allegri's men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace.
Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men.
Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku.
Fenerbahce suffered another setback after last week's humiliating 6-0 loss at Aston Villa, blowing a two-goal lead to be held 2-2 at home by Slavia Prague.
PSV Eindhoven clinched their first victory with a 1-0 success at Porto.
f32b341652a2a357: NEW YORK: The Dow rose 1% on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street's biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag.

Healthcare led gains among the S&P 500's 11 major sector indexes, hitting a record high. Eli Lilly was the S&P 500's biggest index point contributor while UnitedHealth, Merck & Co, Johnson & Johnson and Amgen helped boost the blue-chip Dow industrials.

Declines in megacap stocks pulled down the communication services sector. Energy shares underperformed as oil prices fell after touching a five-month high. Oil traders were weighing a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a US-Iran mediator, against Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Tech stocks take a breather

While the heavyweight technology sector eased 0.3%, it was the biggest index-point drag on the S&P 500 and kept the Nasdaq close to flat. Technology stocks had rebounded on Monday from a selloff last week when investors worried about steep spending and financing costs for AI developments.

"Equity investors are still a little skeptical around the AI trade and the ability for some of these companies to monetise their investments, so you're seeing a bit of a rotation into other areas of the market," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, pointing to advances on Tuesday in small caps and healthcare companies.
"Investors are looking for other opportunities outside of tech, and healthcare is one of the beneficiaries of that," he said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 gained 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82.
The S&P 500 value index rose 0.9% compared with a 0.2% drop in its growth counterpart. The small-cap Russell 2000 index finished up 1.7%.
With a 1% gain, the financial services sector was the S&P 500's second-biggest index point boost. Defensive sectors also outperformed, with real estate adding 1.7% and utilities climbing 1.2%.
A 1.7% drop in Netflix, a 1.6% decline in Meta and a 1% loss in Google parent Alphabet sent the communication services index down 0.9%.
SpaceX reported a third-quarter profit after the market closed that blew past estimates, boosting its shares 4% in late trading.
Netflix issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for fourth-quarter profit after the bell, and its shares fell 6%.
Meta and Tesla are scheduled to report on Wednesday.
General Motors shares sank 6.8% after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales.

3M rose 5.8% after the company said it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon and issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary to purchase 3M common stock worth over US$521 million. The industrial conglomerate also raised its full-year profit forecast.

Credit reporting firm Equifax rallied 11.3% after it reported third-quarter profit above analysts' estimates. Hasbro shares jumped 11.2% after the toymaker raised its full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, where there were 114 new highs and 236 new lows.

On the Nasdaq, 3,245 stocks rose and 1,608 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.02-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 22 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 266 new lows.

dbd29057f8b63649: LONDON: Liverpool stormed back from a two-goal deficit to beat Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield and maintain a perfect start to their Champions League campaign on Tuesday.
Villarreal coach Inigo Perez looked set to get one over on his old boss Andoni Iraola as the Spaniards deservedly took a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona.
But twice the visitors were undone by their failure to defend crosses into the box as Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo levelled before half-time.

Mac Allister fired in his second 25 minutes from time and substitute Florian Wirtz completed the comeback as Liverpool moved alongside Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table with nine points from three games.

Iraola left out all three of his over £100 million (US$133 million) forwards as Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola joined Wirtz on the bench with one eye on the visit of high-flying Brighton in the Premier League on Sunday.
Villarreal took full advantage of a much-changed Liverpool side early on and were gifted the opening goal after just four minutes.
Virgil van Dijk miscued his attempted header back to Alisson Becker and Mikautadze finished coolly from close range.
Perez's own managerial career got started by chance when he was denied a work permit to join Iraola as his assistant at Bournemouth.
Instead he ended up as boss at Rayo Vallecano, where he had previously worked under Iraola, and led the La Liga minnows to the Conference League final last season.
Perez's knowledge of Iraola's system was clear as Villarreal opened up Liverpool at will at times during the first half.
A fine team move finally led to a second goal when Nathan Saliba picked out the run of Cardona from left-back and he steered the ball past Alisson.
Liverpool's understudies in attack had barely threatened until Mac Allister's looping header from a Kostas Tsimikas corner kickstarted the fightback.
Rio Ngumoha then began to tease the Villarreal defence but the first of two assists for the 18-year-old owed a lot to poor defending.
Cardona let Ngumoha's cross go at the back post, unaware that Araujo was steaming in to head in the equaliser.
That was the Uruguayan's last act as he made way for Wirtz at half-time and Liverpool clicked through the gears after the break.
Ngumoha's searing pace down the right wing opened up the Villarreal defence and his low cross was smashed in off the underside of the bar by Mac Allister.
Just three minutes later Cody Gakpo picked out Wirtz to score his first goal of the season and hit back at his critics over a lack of end product.
Iraola's men remained suspect at the back, though, and Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish with a sweet connection to Ayoze Perez's cross.
But Liverpool held on to close in on the last 16 and leave Villarreal on just three points from their first three games.

ed8c925ab4679c8a: Given that water is 1,000 times denser than air, moving through those two mediums requires very different mechanics—or so one might assume. Yet birds like gulls and puffins can plunge into the sea, swim underwater, and leap back into the air to fly away. And now engineers at MIT and EPFL in Lausanne, Switzerland, have designed a robot that can do likewise.

The “flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle,” or FAAV, weighs less than 300 grams (about half a pound) and is equipped with a central fuselage, two flexible wings, and a steerable tail. The body contains a battery and a waterproof electric motor that drives a crankshaft, which pumps the wings up and down at preset frequencies. The wings are made of thin membranes that are coated with hydrophobic nanoparticles to help wick away water. And the tail is motorized, enabling it to change its angle to help the robot fly up or dive down.

In experiments carried out in a water tank and at Lake Geneva, a team led by Raphael Zufferey, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT, identified combinations of wing size, flapping frequency, and tail angle that enable the robot to smoothly transition from swimming to flying.

The best results came with medium-size wings that were flexible enough to minimize flapping amplitude in water and also firm enough to keep the robot aloft in the air. The speeds and flapping frequencies were similar to those used by actual birds, and a pitch of 70 degrees—a relatively steep angle—allowed the robot to make the leap from water to air. Interestingly, although many diving birds paddle their feet to help them take off from the water’s surface, the team found that the bot didn’t need feet at all.
The engineers’ results could help pave the way for a new class of drones and vehicles that could fly to and sample from aquatic regions too dangerous for traditional vessels to access.

“Our dream vision is for oceanographers, marine biologists, and members of coastal communities to launch this robot from a boat, or from shore, and it would fly close to the area of interest, such as an iceberg or a port facility, or over a pod of whales,” says Zufferey. “It would dive into the water to take a measurement or collect a sample, and fly back to deliver the data at a fraction of the cost of traditional methods. Then it could go back out to dive for more.”

The researchers are now trying to design wings that can turn as well as flap. They will also test the robot’s performance under turbulent conditions, such as swimming in choppy waters and flying through wind. Then they hope to deploy the vehicle to help answer questions in ocean science.

“One of the major challenges in ocean science is collecting data both frequently and across many locations, which is something this robot could do in the future,” Zufferey says. “You could send this out not just every week, but every hour. It could fly out at high speeds, dive in, fly back, deliver its data, and go back out, multiple times.”
cbd492585e405940: When Tristan Brown, an associate professor of history at MIT, first examined a Chinese tea chest label displayed at Old South Meeting House, he had no reason to doubt its story. Descendants of the Boston blacksmith Thomas Wells had donated the label in 1987, saying it had been recovered after colonial protesters threw tea into Boston Harbor in 1773.

But after a year of research, Brown reached a different conclusion: The label was made nearly a century later. The decisive clue came when he read the Chinese text in Cantonese rather than Mandarin, as previous scholars had done. He found that the characters had been used phonetically, in slightly variant forms across contemporary sources, to represent the name of Smith, Archer & Co., a US firm that acquired Asian tea for shipment to American markets during the 1860s and 1870s.

Working with the Wells family, he traced the label to a relative who traveled from Michigan to California during the Gold Rush era before returning and operating a business known as the California Tea Store. Brown argues that claims for its revolutionary pedigree probably developed later, amid the centennial commemorations of the 1870s.

The discovery does not make the label historically insignificant, he says. Instead, what began as an inquiry into a supposed artifact of the Boston Tea Party became a study of how ordinary objects acquire historical authority, and how historical memory itself is made.
“History is never finished,” he says. “Even objects that have sat in museums for decades can reveal entirely new stories when we ask new questions.”
13c1c4e279bd4f5f: The average American throws out around 81 pounds of clothing each year, and there are few options for recycling it. MIT engineers hope to cut down on that textile waste with a new type of yarn.

The thermoplastic yarn mimics the properties of conventional elastic yarns, which typically combine spandex with polyester or nylon. But the MIT team found a way to create a similarly stretchy yarn from two variations of polyethylene, a material commonly used in milk jugs and grocery bags. 80fa3b99b1846ed4: A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet can help some people lose weight, and some research has shown that it may protect against colon cancer. But a new study suggests that such a ketogenic diet may also increase the risk of cancer in the small intestine.

This type of diet forces the body to burn fatty acids instead of carbohydrates for fuel, producing by-products called ketone bodies. One of these, BHB, was thought to be responsible for the protective effect observed against colon cancer.

Omer Yilmaz, director of the MIT Stem Cell Initiative, worked with colleagues including MIT postdocs Jessica Shay and Fangtao Chi to investigate whether the effects were similar in the small intestine. But instead, they found that mice on a ketogenic diet were more likely to develop tumors in that part of the gastrointestinal system than those on a control diet were.

Additional studies revealed that this tumor growth was driven by the way intestinal cells burn dietary fat for energy—a metabolic pathway called fatty acid oxidation. This pathway activates proteins that signal stem cells to multiply more rapidly.
“Having more stem cells means that when you injure the small intestine, it can repair itself better, but the downside is that having more active stem cells can lead to tumor formation,” Yilmaz says.

Though the researchers confirmed that a ketogenic diet suppressed the development of colon tumors, their findings suggest that ketone bodies are not involved. “These molecules are essentially metabolic bystanders,” Yilmaz says.

One implication is that commercial ketone supplements probably do little to either help or harm people who take them. But the deeper issue is “why the same diet has opposite consequences in two adjacent parts of the gut,” Chi says. “That is what we are working to understand next.”
Whatever they discover, as Yilmaz says, “the message here is that we need to be very careful in generalizing the effects that these diets can have.”

fb901bce566f04be: More than 11 percent of the GPUs at Meta’s Prometheus supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, are either dead or sitting idle waiting to step in when the next drops out, Zuckercorp revealed this week.
The massive pool of redundant GPUs is just one of several measures the hyperscaler has taken to keep its AI training runs on track.

Prometheus is among Meta's largest compute deployments to date. Powered by Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and (soon) Vera Rubin rack systems, Meta says the supercluster will eventually scale to a gigawatt of capacity spanning about a million accelerators.
But as anyone who has worked on a large scale compute cluster understands, whether for LLM training or traditional HPC workloads, more chips inevitably means more problems.

In an eight-GPU node, the chance of having a GPU fail is relatively low. In a 100,000-GPU cluster, failures are unavoidable. Meta is building something that's 10x larger and requires distributed training runs across multiple datacenters. Keeping the entire thing humming long enough to reach the next checkpoint becomes a major headache.
In a blog post published this week, Meta offered a unique look at the work it's done to keep failures from derailing the development of models like Muse Spark or its most recent release Muse Wonder.
Idle GPUs are the cost of continuity
When Meta began the first phase of its Prometheus deployment in New Albany, the company says, it was experiencing roughly 1,000 interruptions per day for every 8,000 GPUs.
Interruptions don't mean GPU failure. They simply mean something crashed, failed, or timed out, forcing the training run to stop and roll back to the last known good checkpoint.
Meta claims in the year since it's been able to cut down the number of interruptions by 99 percent, to about 11 per day per 8,000 GPUs.

One of the ways it's done this is by keeping some of Prometheus' GPUs in reserve. The cluster is currently powered by a combination of GB200 and GB300 systems, each with 72 GPUs per NVLink domain. However, only 64 of them are ever in use at any given moment. The other eight are essentially hot spares.

Meta did this because a single failed GPU would take out an entire rack and interrupt the training run. Now, when a GPU fails, one of the spares can slot in and take its place. While this saves time — Meta doesn't have to drop the entire rack from the cluster or wait for someone to swap the faulty component to start training again — a failed GPU would still result in an interruption, albeit a shorter one.
Parallel resiliency
To mitigate this, Meta took advantage of the fact that large scale training jobs usually use data parallelism, where multiple copies of the model are resident within the cluster.

"When a fault can be isolated to a data-parallel model replica, we reduce the impact of a hardware failure by allowing a single faulty replica to be taken offline, while the remaining cluster repeats that step and continues productive training," Meta explained. "The compromised slice simply restarts on available spare hosts and resynchronizes, converting a potential total system halt into a minor, temporary reduction in aggregate throughput."

In other words, Meta's training runs only get interrupted if the fault exceeds the data parallel domain. When this happens, the company has implemented a comprehensive checkpointing scheme, which you can think of a bit like auto-save or a revision history. That way if something does fail, Meta doesn't have to start over from scratch.
"Our distributed checkpointing architecture asynchronously saves the model state — including gradients and optimizer data — to multi-tier storage," the company wrote.
NVLink growing pains

Meta says one of the most difficult challenges was making the NVLink fabrics used to connect 72 GPUs behave like one great big accelerator. Earlier H100 and H200-based systems featured just eight GPUs per NVLink domain, which meant the links were far shorter and less numerous. But this functionality was expanded nine-fold with Nvidia's Blackwell generation.
"With over 600,000 NVLink connections, even marginal signal degradation triggers frequent NVLink recovery cycles," the company wrote.
To overcome this, Meta had to implement a continuous telemetry system and conduct L11 diagnostic burns to isolate weak links before the systems were put into production.

Power was another challenge. Ramping up and down tens of thousands of GPUs for a training run can introduce massive spikes in power consumption called transients, which can overwhelm power supply equipment.

According to Meta, by focusing on the stability and reliability of its cluster, it was able to achieve more than 85 percent "goodput" — a measure of useful throughput — for pretraining and more than 90 percent for reinforcement learning on its latest model Muse Wonder.

The company's ambitions don't stop here. As it works its way toward a million GPUs, Meta hopes to get its interruption rate down to just two per day for every 8,000 GPUs, or about 100,000 GPU-hours mean time between interrupts. ®

b8de06d2e0046246: OpenBSD 8.0 is here, marking the project's 61st release and continuing its schedule of semiannual releases dating back to 1996. What started more than 30 years ago as a fork of NetBSD has grown into one of the most security-conscious operating systems in active development. In a post to the project's announcements mailing list, OpenBSD founder Theo de Raadt highlights a host of improvements included with the latest version and writes that the project remains "proud of OpenBSD's record of more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install."

The latest OpenBSD version brings new features and improvements across the board. These changes, particularly the new Intel Arc support and expanded virtual address space, should improve compatibility with modern graphics cards and allow the system to map more than 4GB of VRAM. Some of the major updates noted in the release newsletter are as follows:
Added support for Intel Arc A-Series (DG2/Alchemist) graphics cards.
512GB kernel virtual address space on AMD64, up from 4GB, allowing VRAM mapping above 4GB.
Added hibernation support for ARM64 systems.
RISC-V improvements including kernel support for the 'V' vector extension and support for Advanced Interrupt Architecture.
Wireless network driver additions and improvements, including 802.11n and 40 MHz channels for the qwx(4) wireless driver.
Added support for up to 64 virtual CPUs per guest virtual machine.
Security and internal improvements for LibreSSL 4.4.0 and OpenSSH 10.6.
Improvements to the vmm/vmd virtualization stack.

The new OpenBSD also retires support for Loongson architecture after the port stopped working with the Clang 22 compiler. If you're interested in reading over all the changes that come with the new OpenBSD 8.0, you can take a look at the release announcement.
c645704d900cbbad: Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet.

There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices.

The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here - Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide.

6300bdf6f44d244c: Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse.

Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn't very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we'll need to run complex algorithms, we'd have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit.

On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10.

b21ea78343004fa2: Multiple ransomware groups, including Qilin and Inc, have been exploiting a high-severity authentication bypass bug in Palo Alto Networks' PAN-OS, with Unit 42 investigating attacks since early June across numerous industries, such as finance, healthcare, and manufacturing.
CVE-2026-0257 affects PAN-OS GlobalProtect portals and gateways, potentially allowing attackers to bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorized VPN connection.

The security vendor first disclosed and patched the bug on May 13 and initially assigned it a medium-severity rating, saying it was aware of attempts to exploit it but had not observed any malicious exploitation.
That assessment quickly changed, and by the end of the month, Rapid7 researchers said they observed successful exploitation across multiple customer environments dating back to at least May 17.
On Monday, Palo Alto Networks’ consulting and incident response biz, Unit 42, said ransomware crews including Qilin and Inc continue to batter the CVE.

“Attackers are leveraging this vulnerability to gain an initial foothold into corporate networks, subsequently bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA) controls to establish a VPN session,” said Andy Piazza, a senior director of threat intelligence at Unit 42.

After gaining initial access, the criminals move laterally across the networks using Remote Desktop Protocol and Server Message Block (SMB), dropping additional malware for credential harvesting and data theft before ultimately deploying ransomware, Piazza warned.

In its ongoing investigations, Unit 42 has spotted the ransomware criminals infecting “numerous industries, including education, financial services, healthcare, high tech, hospitality, manufacturing, professional and legal services, government, transportation and logistics, utilities and energy, and wholesale and retail."
Palo Alto Networks did not respond to The Register’s inquiries about the attacks, including how many organizations have been infected.

Additionally, ReliaQuest intel analysts warned that “multiple threat groups,” including Settra ransomware operators, are also exploiting the bug to gain initial access to corporate networks via unauthorized VPN sessions.

“The most significant evolution in tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs) following successful exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 is the direct pivot to the virtualization layer,” Piazza wrote. “In one notable case, attackers moved from the compromised VPN gateway to the vCenter management appliance. From there, they disabled security controls on ESXi hypervisors (execInstalledOnly) and used a custom tool to perform offline credential dumping directly against a domain controller's virtual disk (VMDK).”
This allows the miscreants to bypass in-guest endpoint detection and response products, and represents “a highly sophisticated method” of stealing domain-wide credentials, he added.
Unit 42 has also spotted criminals chaining this exploit for initial access with other vulnerabilities such as CVE-2023-27532, which targets Veeam backup infrastructure.

So if you haven’t already patched vulnerable PAN-OS software, do so now - and investigate whether attackers have already gained access to your network. Check Unit 42’s indicators of compromise to assist with threat-hunting activities.®

23356c532d0e1e80: An "avalanche of vulnerability reports" is forcing curl to move lower-severity cases into public view, reserving private handling for high and critical flaws.
From October 26, low and medium-severity reports should be filed in the open source data transfer tool's public GitHub repository, maintainer Daniel Stenberg said.

"Security researchers in doubt can still submit the issue on HackerOne and we can tell them what severity we deem it to be. Over the last few years, over 90 percent of all submissions could quickly be assessed to be less than HIGH."
Stenberg already shuttered curl's bug bounty scheme this year as AI-generated submissions piled work onto its security team.
Stenberg has previously acknowledged that not all AI-assisted reports are bad, but the workload now demands another response.

"This policy change is entirely triggered by the current avalanche of vulnerability reports that keep pouring in. We see no end to them and we do not anticipate this flood to decrease within the next several months.

"We are struggling as a project as all key maintainers feel strained, overloaded and brought to the brink of what we can muster. We must act to survive. This is our next step in a survival strategy. It might not be our last. We aim to not drown."
Public handling would let more people assess reports, develop fixes, write advisories, and check for related problems before releases ship, Stenberg said.

Handling vulnerability reports publicly won't reduce the work per report, he admits, though it could spread the load and make the resulting lessons and documentation easier to find. At least that's the theory.
Public disclosure also gives attackers more time to exploit flaws before fixes arrive. The maintainer agrees this is unfortunate yet unavoidable.
"We limit this practice to less than HIGH for this reason: at least these problems are not terrible."
Stenberg said researchers using AI are generating unusual option combinations unlikely to occur in real applications, then treating minor discrepancies as vulnerabilities.

"We can't continue down this spiraling path with our sanity intact. We don't have the bandwidth, manpower or even will to handle a never-ending vulnerability reporting stream at this pace. I believe few software projects can stand this kind of prolonged high volume deluge for extended periods. Something needs to give way." ®

e683e8056bf173c6: AS of now, 6.12 billion people, or 74 per cent of the Earth's population, use the Internet for communication, entertainment, education and work.
Once concentrated on messaging, banking, news, navigation, blogging, gaming and social media, video and music streaming platforms have made huge strides and drawn billions of subscribers.
Two billion more use the Internet for virtual classrooms while about 3.5 billion of the global workforce uses it for corporate communications and the knowledge and gig economies.

The Internet is the top wealth generator of this era, and now the true workhorses powering it have emerged: 12,260 data centres spanning 180 countries, some in town-like warehouses, some buried underground or inside cavernous mountains, and some hidden undersea.

The United States operates the most with 5,430 facilities, or 45 per cent of the global infrastructure, followed by the United Kingdom (564), China (443), Germany (532), France (391) and India (298). Malaysia is modestly catching up: 26 operators across 64 facilities, including those already operational, under-construction and planned.
From 2021 to this year, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority reported data centre investments of up to RM386 billion.

But in the US, the US$10 trillion artificial intelligence (AI) boom is roiled with project delays, panicky investors and a massive public backlash that might influence next month's midterm elections. There are already spirited protests against data centres worldwide, Malaysia included, over their effects on the environment, resources and energy degradation.

Here, the public, watchdogs and civil society have urged the government to ban data centres near residential areas, fearing that server cooling will siphon water from residential taps and agriculture plots.
Communities worry the AI boom will drive up electricity bills and stress the national grid, especially due to centres built near houses and schools.
By 2035, data centres are forecast to swallow up one-third of Malaysia's total energy consumption.
This explosive potential growth prompted the drafting of the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill to regulate industry proliferation and shield energy and water supplies.
The bill, spearheaded by the Economy Ministry, will prescribe that investments add economic value while tackling adverse environmental impacts.
Reacting to the backlash, the Johor government rejected 30 per cent of applications for data centres in 2024 for poor sustainability planning and extreme water consumption.

In February, Putrajaya suspended non-AI data centres to conserve resources. While data centres are welcomed, the race to become a regional hub cannot ignore the numerous adverse side effects. Data centres cannot exist at the expense of the environment and infrastructure.
fe50629463dc94be: Microsoft is pruning OneDrive's Copilot options from File Explorer's right-click menu, though the AI assistant isn't being shown the door entirely.

The Windows giant will remove shortcuts for summarizing documents, generating FAQs, comparing files and images, explaining images, extracting text, and asking questions. The rollout begins in mid-November and is expected to finish by early December. "Ask Copilot" will remain.

Microsoft's September 2025 announcement of the feature said: "We are bringing the power of AI directly into your daily file management experience. With just a few clicks, Copilot can help you summarize lengthy documents, generate an FAQ, compare files, or answer questions about your file."

Users can still right-click a OneDrive file and select "Ask Copilot" to start a conversation with the file attached, or use the Copilot icon in File Explorer Home. The individual actions will also remain available in the OneDrive activity center.

Adding a clutch of Copilot options with identical icons did little to make an already crowded menu easier to navigate. In its message on the subject, Microsoft said: "We're simplifying how people use Copilot with their OneDrive files in File Explorer."
An extra click, yes, but at least you won't need a taller screen to view even more context menu options.

Microsoft has stated that it intends to adopt a more thoughtful approach to how and where its AI assistant turns up in its product line. In March 2026, Windows boss Pavan Davuluri said: "We are reducing unnecessary Copilot entry points." File Explorer's crowded right-click menu seems as good a place to start as any.

The File Explorer context menu is also undergoing an overhaul as part of Microsoft's attempt to make it less "cluttered and sluggish," to the point where users could opt to have it work a bit like it used to in Windows 10. ®
2619dd66ca60992a: PARIS: French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu on Tuesday vowed a "massive" police presence at fresh protests called for the coming weekend, as he faced criticism over the handling of recent street violence.

The eurozone's second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to president Emmanuel Macron.
Facing angry lawmakers in parliament, Lecornu acknowledged that the security response had fallen short and promised a stronger approach ahead of a new wave of protests.
"The deployment for next Saturday will be massive," Lecornu said.
He accused ultra-left radical groups of forging an "insurrectionary plan" that led to the riots, which erupted on the sidelines of nationwide protests over the cost of living.

Images of clashes, mobs looting stores and public buildings set ablaze last weekend prompted several countries, including the US, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.
French authorities on Monday announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities, and Lecornu said new curfews would be imposed on Tuesday where needed.
Paris police ordered a temporary ban on people carrying cans or bottles of petrol or gas, after mobs set fire to government buildings and shops last weekend.
'War films'

During the night, a helicopter flew over the French capital's Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a searchlight across the square to monitor compliance with the curfew.
"The sound of a helicopter at one in the morning is a bit oppressive," said Sylvain Courant, a resident of the Les Halles neighbourhood, another hotspot of the street violence.
"It's that thing you see on TV, in all the good war films," Courant said.
Macron, currently on a Gulf tour where he secured additional diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, has acknowledged shortcomings in the handling of the protests.
France's government is wrestling with high public debt and anger over soaring prices, and facing a strong challenge from the far right.
The unrest on Saturday broke out after around half a million people turned out across France to denounce the cost of living, following four weeks of school protests.
On Monday, several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews.
A targeted curfew for minors was to be introduced in several districts of the southern port city of Marseille from Tuesday evening and at least through Friday, a source close to the matter told AFP.
'Wake-up call'
Security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to the ultra-left over the burning down of a historic town hall in Limoges, whose destruction has become a symbol of the violence.

Authorities have come under criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a "wake-up call" that exposed a "profound crisis" of authority.
Investors have sold off French debt in recent weeks amid rising doubts about the government's ability to rein in spending.
Under pressure to support thousands of damaged or looted shops, the government said interest-free loans would be made available from Friday to all affected businesses, along with other measures.
Justice minister Gerald Darmanin said nearly 150 people had been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts.
He argued that a strong judicial response was necessary to prevent ordinary people from taking matters into their own hands.
"The justice system is being extremely firm," he said. "People with no previous criminal record are being sent to prison."
Some demonstrators were seriously injured. One man lost a hand to a police grenade. In the eastern city of Mulhouse, a 17-year-old girl lost an eye.
Interior minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday, saying police "had lost control" during the unrest. Macron rejected his resignation.
Troops in Milan
Other European countries have also seen demonstrations over rising prices, with smaller clashes breaking out in Milan, Italy's financial centre, and Belgium over the weekend.
Italy was preparing to send 500 troops to Milan as the government considered a wider crackdown.
US president Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, as his Republican party faces strong headwinds in the upcoming midterm elections.
"It's immigration, and I told president Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders," said Trump.
Several analysts countered that immigration was not a driving force in France's unrest.

481036bb5c740fdb: MILAN: The production of Italian pasta is under threat as a protest by truck drivers in the south of the country over soaring fuel prices and the cost of living blocks deliveries to factories.
There are also growing concerns about food supplies in Rome, as transport bottlenecks hamper deliveries from southern Italy to the capital.
Italian agriculture lobby group Confagricoltura warned that producers in Sicily would have to destroy large quantities of perishable products if transportation did not resume.
Pasta maker Rummo, based in the Campania region, said on Tuesday it had suspended production after running out of ingredients.

Almost all major pasta producers in the neighbouring region of Puglia, which together with Campania and Sicily form the heartland of Italy's pasta production, are facing similar difficulties, CEO Cosimo Rummo told daily la Repubblica.
"This means that most of Italy's pasta production has ground to a halt, or is close to," he said.

La Molisana, another producer based in the Molise region, said it had experienced a significant drop in production and had been forced to draw on its stocks of raw materials such as wheat and semola flour.
Italy's pasta supply chain last year generated €13.5 billion in revenue, the European House-Ambrosetti (TEHA Group) said in a report in September.

The Centro Agroalimentare Roma (CAR), Italy's largest wholesale fruit and vegetable market, said roadblocks and higher transport costs were causing shortages of products such as tomatoes, peppers and grapes, pushing up prices and increasing reliance on imports from countries including Spain and Albania.
The government is pledging more aid for road hauliers.
After meeting with their representatives on Tuesday, Deputy Infrastructure Minister Edoardo Rixi said a package worth more than €150 million would be made available soon.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration is also preparing a security crackdown in response to weekend riots in Milan and other northern cities, which developed on the back of demonstrations against inflation.

Vincenzo Aleccia, president of the Trapani trucking consortium in the western Sicilian port city, told Reuters that he knew the disruption was enormous but added that "it's a peaceful protest and it's for the benefit of the people," saying rising prices affected everyone.
The protest, which began last week with the blocking of roads, motorways and ports in Sicily and the south, is causing shortages at supermarkets and queues at petrol stations.

"People were trying to grab whatever was left. I had to go to a nearby town, and I also stocked up on flour and the food we consume most," said Zineb Boutimah, 45, who lives in Locri, a town in the southern province of Reggio Calabria.
Elena Lombardo, 78, also from Locri, said her local petrol station attendant had urged her to fill up her tank on Monday, warning, "I don't know whether there will be any petrol tomorrow."
On Tuesday, the petrol station was closed.

7c5d6a77c9ff4d2f: LONDON: Prince Harry has said he hoped to reconcile with King Charles and the rest of his family with whom he fell out when he moved to the US six years ago.

Harry, 42, the king's younger son, caused a huge rupture in the British royal family when he and his wife Meghan quit royal duties and moved to California in 2020 from where they were highly critical of the institution.
He has barely spoken to his older brother, heir Prince William, for years, and his family has only recently met up again with his father.
In an interview with GQ magazine, Harry, who recently relocated back to Britain with Meghan and their two children, said he wanted to patch things up.
'The most important thing is to reconcile'
"With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile," he told GQ.
He said he could understand the fascination with his family's situation as people could relate to it.
"There's sibling disagreements, there's broken relationships between kids and their parents, kids and one parent," he said.
Some people might be inspired by efforts to reconcile and this could help their own relationships.
"And some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out," he added.
Harry's spokesman said those latter comments were not meant as a swipe at William or any other family members.
Harry, the Duke of Sussex, went on to tell GQ that while "scars stick around forever", he wanted to encourage everybody to let go of the past.
"For me, there's enough drama in the world and enough drama in people's lives than to continue with issues with family," he said. "It's not worth it," he said.
Harry says children 'loving' UK school
In the lengthy interview, Harry also discussed themes he has previously talked about, such as the impact of losing his mother, Princess Diana when he was 12 and his mental health struggles.
However, he also talked about why he had returned to Britain, saying that being able to put his children in a British school "has meant a lot to me".

"I didn't know how important it was to me. I always thought it was going to be something that we would try and do, but now they've been in school for two weeks. They're loving it and it's just giving them a whole different experience".

He also said he hoped that his fraught relationship with the British press, which partly led to him leaving in the first place and has led to a number of lawsuits against newspaper groups, would now be better.
"My hope is that it will change," he said. "There have been some battles that have been fought, necessarily so. But hopefully we can all draw a line under that.

"As with everything else that's going on in the world, there's aspects of the past that I'm sure all of us, me, my family, some of the British press, that we'd all like to leave behind us and work for the greater good," he said.
f2ab6981ac29ae96: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan melarang penyedia perkhidmatan kecerdasan buatan (AI) menggunakan data kerajaan atau rakyat untuk melatih model AI mereka, kata Menteri Digital, Gobind Singh Deo.
Menurutnya, perkara itu merupakan klausa dalam semua kontrak perolehan AI kerajaan dan syarikat AI juga tidak dibenarkan menyimpan data rakyat Malaysia selepas proses pemprosesan selesai.

"Garis Panduan Pengadaptasian AI Sektor Awam (GPAISA) juga mewajibkan agensi meminimumkan data serta menyembunyikan atau menyahnamakan data sebelum diproses oleh sistem AI," katanya dalam jawapan bertulis di Parlimen.
Beliau berkata, kementeriannya sedang menggubal Rang Undang-undang Tadbir Urus AI bagi memastikan wujud akauntabiliti berkaitan sistem AI.
Beliau menjawab pertanyaan Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) bagaimana kerajaan memastikan data awam yang diproses syarikat penyedia perkhidmatan awan dan AI kekal di bawah kawalan Malaysia.
Hanya data terbuka yang tidak sensitif disimpan di awan luar negara

Gobind menjelaskan kerajaan hanya menyimpan data terbuka yang tidak sensitif dalam perkhidmatan awan berpangkalan di luar negara, manakala data kerajaan diklasifikasikan 'rahsia' atau 'rahsia besar' hanya boleh disimpan di pusat data kerajaan, bukan dalam sebarang perkhidmatan awan dalam talian lain.
Jelasnya, maklumat diklasifikasikan 'sulit' atau 'terhad' hanya boleh disimpan dalam perkhidmatan awan persendirian atau hibrid berpangkalan di Malaysia.
"Bagi data peribadi rakyat yang dikendalikan sektor swasta, pemindahan ke luar negara dikawal di bawah Seksyen 129 Akta Perlindungan Data Peribadi 2010 (PDPA), sebagaimana dipinda pada 2024."

Antara lain, seksyen dipinda itu menetapkan persetujuan daripada subjek data diperoleh bagi pemindahan data peribadi merentas sempadan, manakala bidang kuasa negara penerima juga mesti mempunyai undang-undang setara dengan PDPA Malaysia.

Gobind berkata, kerajaan turut mewajibkan penyulitan (enkripsi) terhadap data miliknya bagi memastikan penyedia perkhidmatan asing tidak dapat membaca kandungan data itu secara sepihak, walaupun jika diminta pihak berkuasa negara lain.
29584844a18ef934: OVER the past couple of weeks, a cybersecurity researcher watched as a Chinese-speaking hacker broke into websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including farm equipment maker Deere, home appliance company SharkNinja and engine manufacturer Cummins .
Yet the hacker did almost none of the work.

The cybercriminal instead outsourced the hacking spree almost entirely to artificial intelligence (AI), tasking AI agents with spending hours autonomously probing and breaking into targeted sites, according to Snorre Fagerland, principal threat researcher at the cybersecurity company NorForge.
Fagerland said the hacker was one of several he discovered while scanning the web for inadvertently exposed instances of Cairn, an open-source AI problem-solving platform popular with hackers.

Beginning around Oct 2, Fagerland found about two dozen instances of Cairn being used for malicious activity, which allowed him to quietly peer over the cybercriminals' shoulders as they set their AI tools loose on the world.

At a time of rising anxiety over the power of autonomous AI tools, Fagerland said his find was real-life evidence that commercially available AI agents could pull off complex intrusions from start to finish without human intervention, a dramatic boost to the power of a single malicious actor.
"It's a new world now," said Fagerland.
Reuters could not ascertain the degree to which the breaches resulted in unauthorised extraction of data.
Deere said it had taken "necessary remediation actions" following the incident and had "no indication that sensitive information was accessed".
SharkNinja said the hack had hit a standalone site carrying only product support information and that the threat had been contained.
Cummins said it was "investigating the report of a potential cyber-attack on a website operated by one of our third-party vendors".
Two smaller businesses also acknowledged being compromised. Other victims listed in the Cairn data did not return messages.
One of the hackers that Fagerland observed stole a trove of credit card data. Another tried to get AI agents to rob a cryptocurrency exchange.
The Chinese-speaking hacker was the most prolific. Beginning on Sept 25, they set their AI army loose against American, Canadian, Australian and Japanese e-commerce websites.
Their instructions were terse, sketching out their preferred intrusion tactics in fewer than 100 Chinese characters.
As of late last week, their agents had attempted to break into more than 1,200 sites. Successful intrusions typically took around 23 hours of poking and prodding for vulnerabilities.

Fagerland estimated that the campaign, which appeared to be using a mixture of China's DeepSeek and Anthropic's Claude Code, had chewed up roughly US$5,000 worth of tokens, or about US$50 per successful hack.
Fagerland — who has worked in cybersecurity for nearly three decades — was impressed by some of the techniques the agents used to compromise their victims.

In one case, after failing to find any weaknesses in a big company's public-facing application, the AI agents pored through digital records to find associated infrastructure, located a public-facing control panel, discovered a subtle weakness in the way it processed data, and after hours of trial and error, trick the server into executing malicious commands.
"It's not straightforward to come up with solutions like that," said Fagerland. "It's not script kiddie stuff."
Cairn's author, whose social media handle is "le1xia0", acknowledged receipt of a Reuters message but did not immediately answer a list of questions.

In a recent post on X, they said their platform was "an innovative type of multi-agent architecture and was not designed for hacking attacks. If it is used to carry out harmful hacking attacks, that is not the intention".
The ability of agentic AI systems to autonomously discover vulnerabilities, conduct intrusions, and steal data is a source of increasing anxiety around the world.
Rogue agents have hacked their way out of computer labs, broken into government websites, and engaged in unsanctioned social engineering attempts.
South Korea and Japan have in recent weeks been buffeted by well-publicised hacks attributed to AI-using cybercriminals.
Last week, the cyber intelligence company Bitsight said discussions about how to use autonomous agents were surging across cybercriminal forums.
Fagerland said he had previously assumed hacker-agents would need at least some supervision but it was now obvious that the technology had moved past that.
The writer is from Reuters

d03d74b1ab187f96: KUALA LUMPUR: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) transactions rose 22.5 per cent to RM14.7 billion in the first half of this year, according to figures disclosed in a written parliamentary reply.
The transactions totalled nearly 174 million, up 23.9 per cent from the same period last year.
Buletin Utama TV3 reported that active BNPL account holders increased 22.7 per cent to 9.2 million, while outstanding financing reached RM6.6 billion.

63d3123a5caf3b98: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has proposed that the World Health Organisation's Western Pacific Regional Office (WPRO) urgently pilot a pooled procurement project for selected medicines to strengthen drug security across the region.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal was urgent as countries across the region faced critical challenges from supply chain disruptions, market uncertainty and heavy reliance on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), with geopolitical conflicts worsening the situation.

"Regional diplomacy and solidarity today must be translated beyond mere expressions of good intentions. To protect the survival of health systems in the Western Pacific, we demand a strategic, bold shift in action focused on tangible, measurable results," he said in a Facebook post today.
Dzulkefly presented the proposal at a ministerial roundtable held in conjunction with the 77th WHO WPRO Regional Committee Meeting.
He said the pooled procurement pilot should cover selected medicines with sufficient supplier competition and clearly established shared needs, and be implemented transparently.

To support the mechanism, Dzulkefly proposed developing an Asean Medicines Security Dashboard as an early warning system linking pricing information with supply distribution, stock availability and manufacturing capacity.
He stressed that price monitoring alone could not guarantee medicine security.
Instead, he said the region needed a strategic manufacturing alliance, supported by joint investment initiatives, to address production gaps.
"To realise this major framework, it requires clear leadership from a lead country under the 2026-2030 Plan, complete with funding accountability and clear key performance indicators," he said.

At the domestic level, Dzulkefly said Malaysia had institutionalised pooled procurement across government health facilities, maintained a 3-month buffer stock of medicines and spearheaded the Asean Drug Security and Self-Reliance (ADSSR) initiative.
He added that Malaysia would continue to leverage global health diplomacy platforms to ensure uninterrupted treatment for the public.
bae49355d6c4e904: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Penerangan Parti Wawasan Negara, Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal, mendakwa Bersatu 'tikam belakang' Perikatan Nasional (PN) berikutan keputusan Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM) membatalkan pendaftaran PN.

"Pengkhianatan ini bukan lagi rahsia kerana Bersatu sudah pun melutut kepada Pakatan Harapan (PH)," menurut kenyataan.
