ae74a8939d7a36bf: UPDATED Google Cloud has blamed a “power event” for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe, and is pledging to restore normal service within the hour.
The unplanned downtime for customers began at 0608 UTC when europe-west-2-b, one of three local availability zones in the London region, started playing up.

According to an update on its status page, Google Cloud said at 1158 UTC that full recovery workloads should be “completed, tentatively” by 1300 UTC. Customers can expect another update at that point, with Google either giving the thumbs up, thumbs sideways or having to admit engineers are still working on a fix.

Services that went AWOL included BigQuery Data TransferService, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, Google Kubernetes Engine, and Managed Service for Apache Kafka.
So what caused online services to melt at customers including Lloyds Bank, HSBC, Royal Mail, Rightmove, DPD, BT, Screwfix and Revolut? Power.

"A power event caused an outage within europe-west2-b zone. The power event is mitigated. We are seeing the recovery of services and are prioritizing the recovery of existing workloads.Customers may not be able to yet create new workloads."
The Register has asked Google for further elucidation but it said the only information is available on the status page.

The "fragility" of the cloud model is again on display, Dr Amro Al-Said Ahmad, a lecturer in computer science at Keele University told The Register. He estimates that a total of 38 services were down and out for the count.

"The incident highlights the dependency effect of modern cloud ecosystems. When a core cloud region experiences failures, the impact extends far beyond the directly affected services. Applications, APIs, databases, authentication systems, payment platforms, analytics pipelines, and third-party SaaS products that depend on those services can all experience cascading failures."

"A problem in a single cloud region can therefore propagate through an entire digital supply chain, affecting organisations that are several layers removed from the original outage. While this is a regional outage centered on europe-west2, the breadth of affected services highlights a key cloud engineering lesson: resilience is not achieved by simply moving to the cloud. True resilience requires designing for regional failures through multi-region deployments, workload portability, and tested disaster recovery procedures."
Updated at 17.37 UTC on October 20, 2026, to add:
Google's status page says it mostly ironed out the wrinkles at 14.03 UTC and normal service resumed for the majority of customers.

"The issue with impacted GCP products has been mitigated for most of the customers and it is believed to be affecting currently a very small number of customers and our Engineering Team is working on it."

"No further updates will be provided here. We will publish an analysis of this incident once we have completed our internal investigation. We thank you for your patience while we're working on resolving the issue." ®

add383da2fc04409: Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it's suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.

Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that's required

Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. 372ac744cf74880e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.

1720036ee4831cc8: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a “tough” question during the i-Future programme.

81f7924e4a9c0a89: MADRID, Oct 20 — Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho today warned Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior and the team’s other stars that no-one is “untouchable”.
Vinicius has struggled for form this season and is serving a four-match ban in La Liga for hair-pulling, but is available as Madrid host RB Leipzig in the Champions League tomorrow.
Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, the club’s record €140 million (RM640 million) signing, has impressed in recent weeks, scoring against Sevilla on Sunday in La Liga in Vinicius’s absence.
“Only the club badge is untouchable,” Mourinho told reporters when asked if Vinicius’s place in the team was in danger given Diomande’s form.
“I don’t like the concept of untouchable players.
“What makes a player untouchable is not his status, the armband, his years at the club, how much was paid for him, what makes him untouchable is his performance on the pitch.”
Mourinho said Vinicius would play on the left wing against Leipzig and he had not yet told Diomande whether he would start as well.

Madrid host the Bundesliga side aiming for a third Champions League victory from three matches in the league phase, but in La Liga they are third and six points behind leaders Barcelona, who they visit on Sunday.
Mourinho said the team’s level is still a long way from where he hopes he can take it.
“A long way off... we’ve been here three or four months, it’s impossible to be where we want to be,” continued the veteran Portuguese coach.
“We always have to improve, be it individually or collectively... I understand the demands (at this club) are the maximum.
“I’ve been here three years (2010-2013), and so I know perfectly well how things are. I can’t lose my direction... (even though) I know there is a lot of work to do.”
French defender Ibrahima Konate said the former Chelsea and Manchester United coach commanded respect.
“He’s a great manager, I think he has this aura that not many managers have, because he doesn’t need to speak and everyone will listen and respect him,” Konate told reporters. — AFP
3d3a13a195c627dc: OSLO, Oct 20 — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Oslo today for talks with top US envoys in a bid to get strained relations with Washington “on a more constructive path”, Oslo said.
“We are maintaining all contacts that can help bring peace,” Zelensky said in a social media post announcing his arrival in Oslo.

Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said earlier that Oslo would host talks between Zelensky, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner — the latter taking part remotely — as well as Finnish President Alexander Stubb.

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since President Donald Trump partially lifted sanctions to strike a diesel-supply deal with Russia’s Vladimir Putin and slammed Zelensky as a warmonger for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Zelensky has accused the United States of deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying military aid, saying yesterday that Ukraine received no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes that targeted energy facilities in the capital region.
US-led diplomatic efforts to end Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II have stalled in recent months, as Washington has shifted focus towards the war with Iran.
The Norway talks were due to begin this afternoon and continue into the evening, Store told reporters.
“The aim is to put diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path,” he said.

Ahead of the meeting, Zelensky today said he held “substantive” and “constructive” talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in which he insisted that the US military satellite system Ukraine uses, Starshield, “needs to be restored” and that ballistic missile interceptors “are needed to protect lives”.

Zelensky told US senators yesterday that “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles” already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was waiting for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s signature.
He said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting US approval.
The United States has denied making any changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine, and Rubio today said Washington was not deliberately withholding supplies.
“There’s nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine,” Rubio said while on a trip to India.
“It’s simply, it’s a balance between our obligations to other partners and frankly our own... requirements for our own facilities as well.”

Trump has also denied ordering a reduction in speeds on the US government-owned and -controlled Starshield network after Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said the order could only have come from the White House.
Strained relations
The US leader has accused his counterpart of not trying to resolve the conflict with Russia.
“Zelensky doesn’t know what he’s talking about,” Trump said yesterday.
“To be honest, I think it’s time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine.”

Trump said he was ready to meet Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that talks could also cover the Ukraine war — fuelling fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed earlier that “the topic of such a hypothetical has indeed been mentioned” when asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday that Trump, Putin and Xi could meet.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said that such a meeting would “only encourage Putin to continue this war”.
News outlet Axios reported that Witkoff would travel from Oslo to Russia to meet Putin.

“We hope that it will be possible to arrange a meeting in the very near future, allowing the American negotiators... Mr Witkoff, to brief President Putin on their contacts with both the Ukrainians and the Europeans,” Peskov told reporters today.
Ukrainian authorities said today that Russian strikes killed at least six people around the country, as Moscow targets energy and transport infrastructure with winter approaching.
The attacks came after Zelensky said Kyiv would resume hitting Russian refineries in the face of unrelenting strikes, more than four-and-a-half years into the war. — AFP
e991eca885f8eb35: Bullhorn is the latest tech giant finding itself on the wrong end of a cyberattack, forcing the recruitment software provider to shut down its platform while it investigates.

The US-based company, which serves more than 10,000 customers worldwide, says its systems are now back online in the UK, US, and Australia. Unfortunately for customers hoping to get back to work, online doesn't necessarily mean working.

In its latest status update, published on Tuesday, Bullhorn confirmed that some users were still struggling with single sign-on (SSO), password resets, and customizations, while several products continued to report degraded performance.

Things started going sideways on Friday, October 16, when Bullhorn flagged problems getting job postings onto Indeed. By the following morning, the platform was suffering a full-blown outage, and Bullhorn confirmed later that day that it was dealing with something rather more serious than a technical hiccup.

"We have detected a cyber incident on the Bullhorn Platform. We have temporarily disabled access to our systems in order to contain the activity while we investigate further," the company said, noting that it had roped in cybersecurity specialists from CrowdStrike to help investigate the attack and restore its services.
For recruitment agencies using Bullhorn, the outage meant losing access to candidate records, job applications, placements and, in some cases, the systems used to get people paid.

Services began returning on Monday, but recovery has been anything but seamless. As of Tuesday morning, Bullhorn's status page still listed degraded performance across several products, including its automation tools, Talent Platform, Onboarding365 and Time & Expense.

While Bullhorn is making progress getting customers back into their accounts, it has yet to answer arguably the bigger question: whether the attackers stole anything. In its customer FAQ, it said a forensic investigation is ongoing, and has not yet determined whether attackers exfiltrated customer data.

Bullhorn says it will contact affected customers if the investigation finds their information was compromised, and it also warned people to watch out for opportunistic crooks looking to exploit the chaos.

"Threat actors may pose as Bullhorn personnel via email, text, or phone calls, using the incident as a pretext to request credentials or sensitive information," it warned on Tuesday, stressing that its employees would never ask customers to disclose passwords, multi-factor authentication codes, or verification tokens.
The company has also required password resets for users who don’t log in through SSO, while customers using API integrations have been instructed to rotate their credentials.

The cause of the intrusion remains unknown, and Bullhorn has not publicly identified the attackers or confirmed whether ransomware was involved. The company didn’t respond to The Register’s questions at publication time.
The outage may be coming to an end, but Bullhorn's investigation into what the attackers actually did is far from over. ®

0c4ef484ce9458cc: IPOH, Oct 20 — A local woman suffered losses of more than RM129,000 after being duped by a non-existent online part-time job offer.
Kampar District Police Chief Supt Mohamad Nazri Daud said that his department received a report yesterday from the 34-year-old victim.

“Initial police investigations found that the victim saw an offer for a part-time job related to hotel bookings through social media. Interested, the victim left her phone number to be contacted by the party offering the job.

“The victim received a message from an unknown individual offering the job. The victim was then added to a WhatsApp group supposedly for handling online hotel booking transactions,” he said in a statement today.

Mohamad Nazri said the victim was instructed to make payments for each hotel booking into several bank accounts provided by the suspect, who promised that the capital would be returned along with a commission ranging between 10 to 20 percent, which would increase according to the transaction amount.
He said that due to being lured by the offer and the promise of profits, the victim carried out several money transfer transactions to eight accounts provided by the suspect.
“The victim began to realise she had been cheated when the promised capital and commission were not received after the payments were made. The victim suffered a loss of RM129,975.54,” he said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
7d828c37184d6258: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 individuals per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646).
“The ranking of these four states reflects the extent of drug addiction and abuse that requires attention and targeted intervention.

“Geographical factors also contribute to this situation, with cross-border smuggling routes identified as among the risk factors influencing drug-related problems in these areas,” he said in a statement today.
Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.
He said the statistics were compiled based on integrated data from four main sources, namely Nada, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Health Ministry and private rehabilitation centres.

In this regard, Ruslin said Nada was focusing on enforcement, prevention programmes and community empowerment in high-risk states, targeting three main segments: educational institutions, families and communities.

“A total of 242 prevention and public awareness programmes were conducted, involving 16,408 participants overall, including 228 programmes in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah, which involved more than 16,000 participants,” he said.
He added that 4,253 enforcement operations had been conducted nationwide, with 30,157 individuals detained for treatment and rehabilitation programmes as of last Sunday.

On treatment and rehabilitation, Ruslin said Nada prioritised a voluntary approach, with the average number of individuals seeking treatment on their own initiative rising from 75 a month in 2025 to 232 a month this year.
“This increase reflects positive progress following the implementation of amendments to the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, which came into force on Aug 22, 2025,” he said.

He said Nada would continue to adopt a data-driven approach and strengthen cooperation with state governments through the Drug Eradication Action Council (MTMD) meetings to coordinate prevention, treatment and rehabilitation efforts involving various agencies, families, educational institutions and communities.

4775b1c0b0133fdf: Microsoft has been forced to admit that the Always On VPN glitch – which it said it had fixed in an update on October 13 – was not actually fixed after all.

We've all been there. You fix that bug, or tweak the configuration setting, and you're pleased with yourself, but it turns out it didn't take, and you have to send the "er, about that fix" follow-up email of shame.

The same has happened to Microsoft. After proudly declaring the problem resolved as part of its last security update, the company had to roll back its triumphant trumpeting to a sad little parp from a clown's horn in the message WI1482218:
"This disclosure was mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026. We have returned its status to Mitigated.
"We apologize for any inconvenience or confusion."

The bug in question concerns the operating system's Always On VPN functionality, a useful bit of code that quietly opens a VPN connection in the background without tiresome prompts for authentication. It dates back to Windows 10, and Microsoft alerted administrators to problems after the September 2026 Windows security update inadvertently broke it.
The issue affects Windows 11 versions from 24H2 through 26H2.

The problem could occur when the VPN was set to try a different connection method if the initial connection failed (Microsoft gave the example of using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP).

According to Microsoft: "Affected VPN connections might remain in a 'Connecting' state or repeatedly attempt to connect without succeeding. Subsequent connection attempts might also display the error: 'The specified port is already in use'."

This is not ideal for administrators. The workaround Microsoft highlighted back on October 13 was to change from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, which would at least get affected users up and running.
The workaround remains the same. The bad news is that, because last week's fix did not work, affected administrators will need to apply the workaround for a bit longer.
Microsoft claimed, "A resolution for this issue is planned to be included in an update to be released in the coming weeks." ®
dd88aa55720af9a8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Police have opened an investigation into the circulation of a podcast video alleging that drug trafficking activities were taking place at a house of worship near the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here.

Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the investigation was being conducted under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

“After receiving the Order to Investigate (OTI) from the Deputy Public Prosecutor, police have called several witnesses to assist in completing the investigation,” he said in a statement today.
He said the podcast guest, Azrul Affandi Sobry, will appear at the Sentul IPD at noon tomorrow to have his statement recorded.

422ec2896ed5166b: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks.

He noted that the threat of transnational crime has become increasingly complex due to the misuse of digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), necessitating a faster and more integrated response from Asean member states.
"Asean’s success cannot be measured solely by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the criminal networks dismantled, the victims protected, and the criminals brought to justice.

"This is the commitment that Malaysia is bringing to Manila. Regional cooperation must yield tangible benefits for the security of the people, rather than remaining merely as commitments on paper," he said when delivering the National Statement at the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime (AMMTC) in Manila, Philippines, today.

Saifuddin Nasution noted that Malaysia has outlined three priorities to strengthen Asean cooperation: accelerating cross-border responses to online fraud and illicit financial flows; enhancing investigative capabilities including the handling of digital evidence and asset recovery; and improving operational collaboration between member states and international partners.

He emphasised that the need to expedite such cooperation has become increasingly urgent, given that proceeds of crime can be moved across borders in a matter of minutes, whereas investigative and legal processes typically take much longer.

Consequently, he argued that regional cooperation mechanisms must prioritise the detection of illicit funds, the preservation of digital evidence, and the coordination of investigations to ensure that criminal syndicates cannot exploit gaps in law enforcement between nations.

Saifuddin Nasution highlighted that as Malaysia prepares to chair Asean in 2025, the country has laid a crucial foundation for regional security cooperation through the adoption of the Asean Plan of Action to Combat Transnational Crime (2026-2035) and the Melaka Declaration.

He added that the continuity of these efforts is further reinforced by the Work Programme of the Asean Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC) for 2026-2028, which was adopted last June.
"Currently, our primary challenge is to ensure that all frameworks for cooperation has resulted in tangible actions and outcomes," he said.

Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said Malaysia will continue to play an active role as an Asean voluntary lead country in the areas of money laundering and human trafficking, with the aim of strengthening information exchange, capacity building, and enforcement cooperation among member states.
He noted that Malaysia also hosted the inaugural meeting of the Asean Working Group on Money Laundering in Kuala Lumpur last April, as part of efforts to enhance the coordination of regional actions.

Saifuddin Nasution also shared the measures implemented by Malaysia to address transnational crime, including the establishment of the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) which operates 24 hours a day and can be reached via the 997 hotline since March.

Furthermore, he mentioned that Malaysia has strengthened its cyber-legal framework through the passing of the Cybercrime Bill 2026 in July, and has enhanced border controls by empowering the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency.

He added that efforts to combat terrorism and violent extremism are also being pursued through the Malaysia Action Plan on Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (MyPCVE) 2024-2028, which focuses on prevention, enforcement, rehabilitation, and reintegration. — Bernama
6dfd8590eac72813: BALI, Oct 20 — Asean countries must work together to protect children from growing online threats despite differences in their laws and approaches to internet safety, said Malaysia’s Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said countries in the region shared the challenge of keeping the internet safe for children and needed to strengthen cooperation to address these threats.

“The internet is good. The internet can be put to good use. But do children know how to use it well?” he said in his keynote address at Bali Tech Week 2026, initiated by Indonesia’s Ministry of Communication and Digital today.

Fahmi said Malaysia wanted to ensure that children below the age of 16 were unable to open social media accounts, although approaches to online safety for children could differ between Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and other Asean countries.

Malaysia began enforcing age-verification requirements for social media account registration on June 1 this year under the Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code introduced under the Online Safety Act 2025.

Under the new regulations, individuals under the age of 16 are no longer allowed to open any social media accounts, while those who wish to register must submit official identification documents such as MyKad, passport or MyDigital ID to verify their age.
Fahmi also highlighted the challenges posed by social media algorithms, noting that governments had limited understanding of how they operated and influenced the content users encountered.
At the forum, Fahmi outlined Malaysia’s efforts to improve internet coverage, speed and affordability while making online access safer, particularly for children.

Highlighting the dangers children faced online, he cited a recent case in which Malaysian police apprehended 53 suspected paedophiles and seized more than half a million files suspected of containing child sexual abuse material.
He described online child protection as a challenge faced by countries across the region.
Fahmi also said that governments needed to consider how they shaped people’s choices while ensuring individuals had the freedom to make more informed decisions.

Bali Tech Week, themed “Archipelago Ascending: Advance Together, Innovate Further”, is being held from Oct 19 to 23 at the Bali Beach Convention Centre in Sanur, bringing together policymakers, technology leaders, innovators and investors.
Fahmi was invited by his Indonesian counterpart, Meutya Hafid, to deliver the keynote address at the event during his working visit to Indonesia from Monday to Thursday.
He will travel to Jakarta later Tuesday to continue his official engagements. — Bernama
4f9c53ab978303a9: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed efforts to strengthen the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, positioning it as a hub for the sharing of knowledge and expertise.

“I also emphasised Malaysia’s readiness to share its expertise and expand development cooperation at the international level,” he said in a post on X today.

He mentioned that this was discussed during a meeting today with IsDB president Dr. Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser, reflecting a continued confidence in the nation’s development trajectory and governance.
“God willing, this close collaboration will further enhance Malaysia’s role as a credible development partner, while bringing the expertise of our people to the global stage,” he added.

The IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, launched in 2019, serves as a strategic platform for the transfer of technology, expertise, and best practices in Islamic finance from Malaysia to the 56 other IsDB member countries.

The IsDB, headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, is a multilateral development finance institution established in 1975 to support the economic development and social progress of its member countries and Muslim communities worldwide, based on Shariah principles. — Bernama

5ae5cefb613a38c3: KLANG, Oct 20 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain.
His Royal Highness stressed that royal status did not give anyone the right to act as they pleased, reminding family members to respect the law and comply with all regulations.

“We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. Every family member is accountable for their conduct and actions, as the behaviour of one individual can affect public perceptions of the entire royal family.

“The way we conduct ourselves, interact with society and fulfil our responsibilities must reflect the dignity and integrity of the royal family and institution,” His Royal Highness said at a royal tea reception with members of the royal family in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign at Padang Mahkota, Istana Alam Shah, here today.
Also present were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah and his wife, Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz.
The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.
His Royal Highness said differences of opinion and misunderstandings should be resolved wisely and amicably, without spreading false stories, provoking disputes or making hurtful remarks.
“Be mindful of your words and manners, including when using social media, and practise mutual understanding, tolerance and forgiveness.

“I also urge family members to support and care for one another. We should not gather only for ceremonies and celebrations but also offer help and support when our relatives face difficulties,” the Sultan said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also called for the values of compassion, responsibility and mutual respect between older and younger generations to be nurtured and passed down to future generations.

At the same time, the Sultan also expressed delight at the attendance of nearly 1,200 members of the Selangor royal family, saying the Silver Jubilee celebration provided a meaningful opportunity to strengthen family ties.

“Some of my relatives who are here this afternoon are people I have not seen for a long time, while others belong to the younger generation who have now reached adulthood. Your presence means a great deal to me.

“This gathering not only brings me joy but also reminds us of our shared responsibility to preserve family harmony and the dignity of the Selangor royal institution,” His Royal Highness said. — Bernama
9a21153c99c455a7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed sadness over the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional (PN), describing the development as a lesson for leaders of political coalitions to act fairly towards all member parties and comply with their constitutions and the law.
In a statement, Muhyiddin, who founded PN, said he was saddened by the coalition's deregistration.
"However, this decision is a reminder to any party leading a coalition to act fairly towards all member parties and to always comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966," he said.
Muhyiddin also cautioned against the misuse of power and position within a political coalition for the benefit of a particular party or group.
He said such actions could cause a coalition to drift away from the original objectives and purpose behind its formation.
"Do not misuse power and position in a coalition solely for the interests of a particular party or group to the point where the coalition deviates from its original goals and objectives," he said.
Muhyiddin added that he would discuss the way forward with the Bersatu leadership at a special Political Bureau meeting scheduled for tonight.

Earlier today, the Registrar of Societies announced the deregistration of PN after finding that the coalition's explanation had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.
a41e7d9761454d35: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Students struggling with bullying should seek justice through their schools first before bringing their grievances to the Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB), said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Azalina said the TAB would also evaluate the complaints received before accepting the relevant cases for mediation to prevent it from being overwhelmed with the high volume of complaints.

She said the TAB serves as a deterrence measure, similar to the Anti-Sexual Harassment Tribunal (TAGS) established in March 2024, and would function as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism outside the schools and courts.
However, she also stressed that the TAB is not a substitute for the courts and that it would be impartial to both bullying victims and perpetrators.
“The tribunal looks at both the victim and the perpetrator. So, it is not just going to look at damages or compensations.

“When they issue an award, they will also add in certain assistance on emotional challenges, for example,” she said, after attending the Anti-Bullying Literacy Programme at IPG Kampus Bahasa Melayu, here today.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek was also present at the event.
According to Azalina, the TAB has clocked 68 cases since its launch in June, with adolescents in the secondary schools aged between 13 and 17 students forming the bulk of the cases (42 cases).
Majority of the reported cases were from Selangor and Kuala Lumpur (11 cases).

Azalina said the rising numbers of cases reflect growing awareness on bullying, which she said would eventually reduce bullying incidents as perpetrators would realise that the TAB will hold them accountable.
She said the Cabinet will also look into the possibility of extending the services of TAB to adults aged above 18 facing bullying.
However, she said the ministry would first deliberate the matter with the Higher Education Ministry and the Human Resources Ministry before moving forward.

29c1a61ab8cec165: Britain's national digital ID scheme may be dead, but Whitehall appears to have forgotten to tell the infrastructure.

Despite the government scrapping its controversial plans, officials told MPs on Monday that work continues on GOV.UK One Login, digital wallets, and a growing collection of digital credentials designed to help people prove who they are.

The abandoned scheme was one of Keir Starmer's flagship policies, originally pitched as a compulsory digital ID card to crack down on illegal working. Privacy campaigners weren't impressed, warning of surveillance and government overreach, and ministers eventually made it voluntary before Andy Burnham, decided to bin the whole thing.

But scrapping the scheme hasn't dented Whitehall's digital identity ambitions. Officials told MPs this week that more than 80 types of documents are earmarked for the government's digital wallet, including proof of benefits, driving test certificates, and Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) certificates. That's quite a lot of paperwork for something that's supposedly dead.
The revelations came during a Public Accounts Committee hearing on Monday, where MPs wanted to know what exactly had been scrapped.

"But is it not the case, based on the answers you've given us this afternoon, that the infrastructure of digital ID in the public sector is still being pursued?" asked Sarah Green, Liberal Democrat MP for Chesham and Amersham.

Susannah Storey, DCMS permanent secretary, was keen to draw a line between the national scheme ministers had scrapped and the digital identity projects Whitehall had no intention of abandoning. One Login already allows people to prove who they are online, she said, but "that is not the same as a national digital identity strategy."

Rod Latham, DCMS director for cybersecurity and digital identity, had a convenient explanation for why so much of digital ID was still standing: the government had only scrapped plans for a new identity product.
"We already had One Login and the Gov Wallet," he told MPs, adding that work on the digital identity trust framework was also underway before the national scheme was announced.
Whitehall isn't wasting time putting that technology to use, with officials confirming that testing is already underway to enable digital credentials to work with private businesses.

Natalie Jones, the senior responsible owner for GOV.UK One Login, revealed that the government had opened a testing environment for private sector providers to integrate with its digital wallet technology. This would let people use digital driving licenses to prove their age in pubs, collect parcels, or verify their identity online.

"We've got a bit of a chicken and egg situation. A digital driving license is only useful if there are people ready and shops and businesses ready to receive it,” Jones said, noting that further testing is planned for December, with a national rollout of digital driving licenses targeted for 2027.
MPs also pressed officials on privacy, particularly whether citizens would have to consent before their information was shared between government departments.
"In the confines of digital ID used in digital services, then consent is the model," said Christine Bellamy, interim director general for digital products at the Government Digital Service.
There's a catch, of course. Government departments can already share data without asking permission, and officials couldn't quite explain how that squares with their promises about consent.
"The strategy needs to be fully finished," Bellamy admitted, which might not be the reassurance MPs were hoping for.

Jones insisted that One Login was "not a big data lake," saying it stores identity information separately and cannot see what users do inside government services. "One Login does not issue a single identifier to people," she added.
Rupert Lowe MP remained unconvinced, warning that Britain could end up getting digital ID "by the back door rather than the front door."
Officials maintained that the canceled national scheme was fundamentally different from the services still being developed, and that people would retain alternatives to digital identification.
National digital ID may be officially dead, but between One Login, digital wallets, and dozens of planned credentials, Whitehall still has plenty of identity-related work to keep it busy. ®

67b4bc13ea6833d8: London's mobile network performance has slipped behind other European capitals as operators struggle to add capacity fast enough to meet demand.

The city ranked seventh out of 18 in the continent for median download speed in 2021, but traffic has since expanded faster than available capacity. Other metropolises have improved; London now has the slowest speeds and the highest latency under load, according to mobile network testing firm Ookla.

The research points to obstacles mobile operators face in adding extra capacity: applications for new street masts in London have fallen since 2022, and about three quarters of those filed since 2019 were refused.

The Big Smoke was among the first European capitals to get 5G coverage, yet when Ookla's Q3 2026 tests found the city now has the slowest median download speed (109.43 Mbps), the slowest median upload speed (11.40 Mbps) and the highest latency under load - a measure of how the network copes with heavy use.
Ookla's records show London’s 5G medina speed peaked at 200 Mbps in Q2 2021, fell as low as 102 Mbps in Q3 2023, then recovered slightly. Paris, by contrast, has stayed above 225 Mbps since mid-2021.

The cause is congestion. In Central London, performance slumps on weekdays as commuters arrive: median download speed falls to 80.07 Mbps through the morning, 27 percent below weekend levels at the same hours.
Part of the problem is that UK mobile operators own few of their antenna sites, many of which sit on rooftops in built-up areas, says Ookla.

Under the Electronic Communications Code, and changes introduced in 2017, a London rooftop is worth about £1,000 ($1,333) a year to its owner, down from £21,000 ($28k). That givers landlords little motivation to host antennas, and many prefer solar panels.
Operators can also receive notices to quit when a building is redeveloped, and it is estimated that this keeps about 7 percent of London’s rooftop sites out of action at any time.

Planning rules compound the problem as applications for new masts are more likely to be refused in boroughs with conservation areas, such as Westminster. Street mast applications peaked in 2020, early in the first 5G build, and have fallen by more than four-fifths since 2022. Three quarters of applications for new street masts since 2019 were refused, against one in five upgrades.
"Planning restrictions, particularly in conservation areas, make it harder to install and upgrade the mobile equipment London needs," Ookla lead industry analyst Luke Kehoe told The Register.
"Notices to quit can also force rooftop sites offline during redevelopment long before replacements are ready, leaving operators trying to restore lost capacity while demand keeps growing."

City Hall has noticed, and a draft plan for the capital drawn up by the Mayor of London observes that notices to quit "have eroded London’s overall mobile connectivity compared to other equivalent cities."

The plan, due tor adoption in 2028, would require developers to keep mobile service running during construction, put masts on taller buildings and in the public realm; and ask boroughs to work with operators on sites in conservation areas.

Other experts blame different factors for London’s poor mobile service. Professor Mohamed-Slim Alouini of the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) told The Register last year that the government’s decision to rip-and-replace network equipment supplied by China-based vendor Huawei had diverted funds that should have gone into building more capacity.
He also said 5G was overhyped early on, leading to a perception among users that it wasn’t really worth having and operators reluctant to invest.
Whatever the cause, London’s mobile experience now trails its European peers, though people elsewhere in the UK who still can’t get a 5G signal will have little sympathy. ®
6e1b24106b228477: The UK public sector has reached a cyber resilience inflection point. A new Prime Minister has taken office, and significant machinery-of-government changes have already been announced, including the scrapping of DSIT, the department that had become the center of government digital, technology and cyber policy. Its responsibilities are now being redistributed across other parts of Whitehall, creating a new policy and delivery landscape for public sector leaders to navigate.

For years, cyber security was treated as a specialist operational discipline that was essential but largely delegated to technical teams. That model is no longer sustainable. Pressure is now coming from three directions at once, as policy raises expectations for boards and senior leaders, organizational reform reshapes how services, systems and suppliers connect, and technology change, from cloud and hybrid work to AI, expands both opportunity and exposure.

Together, these forces mean cyber resilience can no longer sit below board level. Public services, from healthcare and benefits to transport, education, local government and emergency response, are now so digitally dependent that a cyber incident is not simply an IT outage. It is a risk to public trust, public safety and the continuity of government itself.

Recent history shows what this means in practice. The 2024 ransomware attack on Synnovis, a pathology services provider to parts of the NHS, significantly reduced the capacity to process blood, urine and specimen tests, caused disruption across south-east London and contributed to delays affecting more than 11,000 outpatient and elective procedure appointments. Incidents like this turn abstract cyber risk into real-world service disruption, making resilience a boardroom issue rather than a back-office concern. Cyber resilience is no longer a technical aspiration, but a leadership obligation shaped by policy, organizational and technology change.
Policy change has made cyber resilience a leadership obligation

The direction from government and the National Cyber Security Centre is clear. The Cyber Resilience Pledge asks organizations to make cyber security a board-level responsibility, register for NCSC Early Warning and take a risk-based approach to Cyber Essentials across their supply chains. The NCSC’s Cyber Governance Code of Practice reinforces the point that cyber risk must be governed like any other material organizational risk. The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill will further expand expectations across essential and digital services, strengthening incident reporting and bringing more critical suppliers into scope.

This matters because the scale and impact of cyber threats facing the UK are increasing sharply. The NCSC handled 204 nationally significant cyber incidents in the year to September 2025, up from 89 the previous year. That means the UK is now experiencing an average of four nationally significant cyber attacks every week.

Policy has therefore changed the boardroom question. Leaders should no longer ask only whether an organization has invested in security tools. They need to ask whether they can prove resilience, evidence accountability and continue delivering critical services when systems are under pressure, suppliers are compromised, data access is disrupted or attackers are already inside the network.
Organisational change is creating hidden cyber risk

The second force is organizational change. Local Government Reorganisation is redrawing structures and responsibilities across England. Rail renationalization and other shifts in public ownership are changing who owns, manages and secures critical data and systems. Departmental priorities and delivery models are also evolving under a new Prime Minister, with DSIT being dismantled and functions including digital transformation, public sector AI adoption, information resilience and online harms moving into different departments and central government structures.

Every one of these transitions creates potential gaps. Systems need to be integrated. Identity and access privileges need to be reassessed. Data needs to move between teams, agencies and suppliers. Contracts and responsibilities need to be redefined. During periods of change, the attack surface expands, and accountability can become blurred.

This is why cyber resilience must be built into public sector reform from the outset. The question is not simply how to restructure services efficiently. It is how to ensure citizens can continue to access those services securely throughout the transition. Reorganization without resilience is a risk to the public.
Technology change demands continuous assurance

The third force is technology change. Public sector work now happens across hybrid environments, shared services, cloud platforms, partner ecosystems and complex supply chains. Traditional security models were built for a more stable world of fixed offices, predictable networks, known users and clearly defined organizational boundaries. That world no longer exists.

AI makes this problem more urgent. AI is already being used across the public sector to improve productivity, analyze information and support better service delivery. But without governance, organizations can quickly lose track of which tools are being used, what data they can access and whether sensitive information is being exposed. Shadow AI is not a future risk. It is a present governance challenge.

Resilience in this environment requires continuous assurance. Access should not be granted simply because a user is on a trusted network. Every request should be verified based on identity, context, device posture and risk. Users should only receive the access they need, when they need it. Applications should be protected from unnecessary exposure. Data should be segmented so that compromise in one area does not automatically spread across the organization.
What public sector boards should do now

Making cyber resilience a board-level priority does not mean every director needs to become a technical expert. It means senior leaders need the right governance, evidence and accountability to respond to the three forces reshaping risk across the public sector. That starts with treating cyber resilience as a standing board agenda item, linked directly to service continuity, citizen trust, regulatory exposure and reform delivery. It also requires boards to understand which critical services depend on which systems, suppliers and datasets, where single points of failure exist, and how disruption in one part of the ecosystem could affect citizens’ ability to access essential services.

Supply chain assurance must be part of that same conversation. Public services are delivered through ecosystems, so resilience cannot stop at the boundary of a single department, council, agency or trust. Cyber Essentials, supplier checks, contractual obligations and clear incident reporting expectations should be embedded into procurement and contract management. At the same time, public bodies need to move away from implicit trust based on networks or locations and towards continuous verification based on identity, context, device posture and risk. Users should have only the access they need, when they need it, and AI adoption should be governed before it scales so innovation does not create unmanaged routes to sensitive information.
Resilience is now a test of public sector leadership

The UK’s policy environment has changed. Public sector organizations are changing. Technology is changing even faster. The only way to manage that complexity is to build cyber resilience into the way public services are governed, transformed and delivered.

The public sector cannot afford to treat resilience as something to retrofit after legislation tightens, reform programs are complete or AI adoption has already accelerated. It must be designed in from the outset, measured at leadership level and tested continuously.

Cyber resilience is not just about protecting systems. It is about protecting the public’s ability to rely on government when policy, organizations and technology are all changing at once. That makes it a board-level priority by definition.

19b0c8a6f51c7c71: A website registered by “David Beckham” was the world’s second-most-visited source of pirated Japanese manga in February 2025, leading publishers to call for better verification of who buys domain names to address the problem.

The “Beckham” who registered the site was of course not the famous footballer and spokesmodel. However Tatsuo Ninoseki, an attorney with the Shin Hirakawa-Cho Law Office who represents the Japan Publishers manga Anti-Piracy Conference (JPMAC), put fake Becks in play today during a session on DNS abuse at ICANN’s annual meeting in Bali, Indonesia.

Ninoseki said miscreants routinely create unauthorized English translations of manga and post them on websites that include ads. The lawyer said such sites can attract hundreds of millions of users and cost publishers $17 billion in revenue each year.

JPMAC has decided its best course of action is not to pursue copyright abusers, but instead to go after commercial-scale pirates. That means it tries to act against pirate websites like those registered by “Beckham,” by sending them stern legal letters and using other legal means.

But those pirates have trained to get around defenders. Ninoseki said pirate manga sites maintain a set of domain names – he said they’ve registered names in 158 top-level domains and frequently “domain hop” between them.

The pirates’ pools of domains include some common naming elements, so even though Google has stopped indexing these pirate sites, users figure out that a theoretical piratemanga.XXX site will soon reappear at piratemanga.YYY.

Pirate sites also redirect from domains they’re not using to host content to another that is full of pirated comics. Sometimes they use several sites at once and direct users across a fleet of live sites, so traffic flows to each site stay small and don’t cause suspicion.

Ninoseki said 82.4 percent of domain hops happen within 15 days of the last move, suggesting pirates know how long enforcement actions or takedown requests will take and move to a different site before they run into trouble.
“Many domain hops do not appear to be a reaction to legal countermeasures,” the attorney said.

Ninoseki said JPMAC feels more comprehensive verification of domain name registrants would be a big help, especially checking physical addresses provided by registrants which he feels would weed out more pirates.
The lawyer spoke during an ICANN session on DNS abuse, which the governance body defines as using domain names to facilitate malware, botnets, phishing, pharming, and spam.

ICANN is currently working on a policy called PDP1 to address DNS abuse, one element of which would require registries to consider all domains held by their customers if just one is found to conduct DNS abuse. 7a9898c01ede12be: If Bersama were to contest 15 seats in the Melaka polls on Nov 14, it is certain to take away votes from PKR, DAP and Amanah.

It is not too late to rescind a move that bodes ill for a future in which Bersama ought to have a vital role in making the reforms long sought by Pakatan Harapan (PH) a reality, thereby setting on course the creation of a different country from the prevailing one, whose contours are likely to be reinforced by the right-wingers of Umno and the Islamists of PAS.

As if the good fairies have decided to play a hand in steering things towards an outcome both congenial for Bersama and beneficial to PH, Bersama’s co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad is in a spot of bother that may well throw him off stride for GE16.

The khalwat case he is facing may well disqualify the former MP for Setiawangsa from being the constituency’s first Bersama MP at GE16. Prior to the case’s inception, Nik Nazmi was on course, after resigning as PKR MP for Setiawangsa, to being returned at GE16, under Bersama’s colours, as the seat’s MP.
Now that probability is dimmed by what hangs over him at the shariah court.

This is grist for the argument that Bersama ought to draw in its tentacles and play to its strengths. There is no point in splitting votes at the Melaka polls and persisting in attacking PKR and Anwar Ibrahim on the stumps, as Bersama has been known to do from the time the party set sail.

When Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi launched a new political vehicle by forming Bersama, it was clear the pair were on course, heading up to GE16, which must be called by February 2028, to carve off something like 10 of the 31 parliamentary seats that PKR won at GE15 in November 2022.
Their incumbents were pro-Rafizi and will likely be won again by the same coterie if re-contested by them.
Bersama will want to contest a number of other seats held by PKR MPs, but not significantly more.

Bersama went into the Johor state polls in July with hopes of making some gains. They wound up with nothing but lost deposits and were suitably chagrined to not want to contest in the subsequent Negeri Sembilan polls.
But now Bersama fancies its chances in Melaka: it has not learnt its lesson that what plays in the Klang Valley does not exactly play outside its highly urban and urbane precincts.
The Nik Nazmi khalwat case is a symptom of Bersama’s presumptuousness.
The party must play within its strengths.
And wait for the realisation to congeal that after Anwar, it is Rafizi who should resuscitate the fallen reformasi colours.
Hence, there isn’t much point in alienating its putative allies in PKR, DAP and Amanah by going solo and splitting votes at the Melaka polls and elsewhere.
What has happened to Nik Nazmi should introduce some grains of sand into Bersama’s balm of complacent assumption.

394cca3f8c173049: ICANN has started testing authentication schemes that will allow law enforcement agencies to make urgent requests for non-public WHOIS information – when needed to address threats to life, critical infrastructure, or child exploitation.

Domain registrars collect information about their customers and in the past that data was publicly available in WHOIS records. Some domain registrars offer services that substitute their own contact details, to preserve customer privacy. In recent years, laws like GDPR mean registrars are sometimes required to hide WHOIS data.

That’s fair enough but makes it hard for law enforcement to contact a domain holder if their resources are being misused – intentionally or otherwise – for purposes such as hosting malware, acting as command-and-control infrastructure for malware, or facilitating phishing.

ICANN’s definition for the kind of behaviour it thinks justifies urgent requests for WHOIS info is “imminent threat to life, of serious bodily injury, to critical infrastructure, or of child exploitation.”

The org has convened an Input Group on Law Enforcement Agency Authentication Mechanisms to consider the issue, and that group yesterday explained its progress during ICANN’s annual meeting in Bali, Indonesia.
At this point, readers may have concerns that this proposal could allow law enforcement authorities to make inappropriate requests for WHOIS information.
Several factors may ease such concerns.
One is that representatives of domain registrars Namecheap and Verisign spoke during the session about the proposal, and both were supportive.

Another is that the Input Group’s work is largely technical. Once it devises a mechanism to allow requests, other groups within ICANN dedicated to policy will work out acceptable use and related issues.

This is the way internet governance gets done! Specialists work on their own bits of a problem and then collaborate to create a robust system that works at a technical level, is practical, and enforceable in multiple jurisdictions.

At this point, ICANN’s preferred approach is to use Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) so that authenticated users at law enforcement agencies can log into the governance org’s Registration Data Request Service (RDRS) and file requests to access non-public WHOIS info. ICANN is already testing this approach with the FBI and Interpol but is open to other authentication mechanisms to allow other agencies access RDRS. The Input Group’s aim is to publish a spec those agencies can conform to.

ICANN will pass requests filed in RDRS to whichever registrar sold the domain. The registrar will have 24 hours to consider the request – or up to 72 hours for complex queries. Registrars will also be able to deny requests if they feel the query does not meet the urgency threshold.
Register readers might worry that a colossal agency like the FBI could flood RDRS with requests from thousands of individual agents, swamping domain registries.

ICANN’s plan is to avoid that by requiring law enforcement agencies to nominate certain personnel who are permitted to make requests, and to enforce that permission using a token shared during SAML handshakes. The content of that token is the kind of policy question that the Input Group expects others at ICANN to finalize later.

Another issue under consideration is how to protect the identity of law enforcement workers who make RDRS requests, as ICANN feels they could become targets of harassment (or worse) if their requests to see WHOIS data include email addresses. ®
6c941b9db65caba4: Hidup berjiran memang ada macam-macam ragam.

Ada jiran yang baik hati, suka menolong, ringan tulang dan mengambil berat tentang orang sekeliling. Ada juga jiran yang kita tidak begitu kenal, tetapi tidak pernah mendatangkan masalah. Masing-masing menjaga hal sendiri.
Ada yang sudah bertahun-tahun tinggal berdepan-depan, tetapi sekadar angkat tangan dan senyum. Tidak pernah berbual. Janji tidak menyusahkan orang lain, kita baik-baik sahaja.
Ada juga yang langsung tidak mahu memandang, apatah lagi bertegur sapa. Tetapi selagi tidak membuat susah kepada orang lain, itu pun tidak mengapa.
Yang susah apabila mendapat jiran yang selalu buat hal. Entah apa penyakitnya, suka membuat orang lain tidak senang.
Laman rumahnya bersemak-samun sehingga mungkin menjadi tempat pembiakan nyamuk. Ditambah pula suka membuat bising tidak mengenal waktu. Sudah tentu kita semua akan rimas dan serba salah.
Apabila ditegur, dia tidak berubah. Silap-silap kita pula diajak bertumbuk.

Bukan dia sahaja yang menyusahkan, seluruh keluarganya pun sama. Anak-anak bukan main nakal, suka mengganggu rakan sebaya. Emaknya pula bermulut jahat, suka mengata sana-sini. Tidak boleh tengok orang lain lebih sedikit, dinaikkan pula hantaran menyindir di media sosial.

Lama-kelamaan, seluruh kejiranan bengang dan terganggu dengan perangai jiran seperti ini sehingga masalah itu terpaksa dibawa ke mesyuarat persatuan penduduk, malah memerlukan campur tangan ketua masyarakat atau pihak berkuasa.
Tetapi masalah tetap tidak selesai. Dia masih tidak berubah.
Apabila ada pihak datang sebagai wakil pendamai untuk memujuk, pandai pula dia mengajar orang lain. Disuruhnya kita bersabar. Katanya, hidup berjiran perlu ada toleransi.

Kemudian dia merengek dan berlakon menjadi mangsa. Orang lain semuanya salah, dia sahaja yang betul. Disebut-sebut dan diungkit-ungkit pula apa yang sudah dilakukannya selama ini. Kononnya dia juga ada jasa di kawasan kejiranan.
Ini bukan cerita rekaan.
Kalau kita tinggal di kampung, rumah pangsa rakyat atau taman perumahan, memang ada orang jenis begini. Kadang-kadang kita pun tidak faham bagaimana orang seperti mereka boleh wujud di muka bumi ini.
Ketika orang lain sepakat dan boleh hidup aman, dia muncul mengocak ketenangan. Apa kepuasan yang dia dapat, kita pun tidak boleh hendak hadam.
Takkanlah tidak tahu bahawa dalam beragama memang ada bab adab hidup berjiran. Kita dituntut supaya menghormati jiran, menjaga hubungan baik dan tidak menyusahkan orang lain.

Tetapi hubungan baik sepatutnya berjalan dua hala. Tidak bolehlah seorang jiran sentiasa diminta bersabar sedangkan jiran yang menyebabkan masalah sewenang-wenangnya melakukan apa sahaja yang dia suka.
Hal-hal mudah pun sepatutnya kita boleh fikir sendiri.
Jangan halang pintu keluar masuk rumah jiran dengan kereta kita. Jangan biarkan haiwan peliharaan membuang najis merata-rata di atas jalan atau di rumah jiran.
Pada musim perayaan, kalau boleh elakkan membakar mercun apabila sudah masuk waktu tidur. Ada anak kecil dan orang tua yang tidak sihat, pasti mereka akan terkejut.
Jangan pula bakar sampah sehingga asap masuk ke rumah jiran.
Ini semua perkara yang kita boleh fikir sendiri.
Tetapi nanti sekejap.
Bagaimana kalau mereka sebenarnya tahu perbuatan itu menyusahkan orang lain, tetapi tidak mempedulikannya?
Lebih teruk lagi jika mereka mendapat keuntungan daripada perbuatan itu, sedangkan orang lain terpaksa menanggung akibatnya.
Ini bukan lagi soal kesedaran atau common sense. Ini sudah masuk soal tanggungjawab.
Rasulullah SAW bersabda, maksudnya:
“Demi Allah, tidak beriman! Demi Allah, tidak beriman! Demi Allah, tidak beriman!”
Apabila ditanya siapakah orang itu, Baginda menjawab:
“Orang yang jirannya tidak berasa aman daripada gangguannya.”
(Riwayat al-Bukhari, no. 6016)

Apabila dikatakan jiran, ia jelas tidak terbatas kepada kaum dan agama. Jiran ialah mereka yang paling dekat di sekeliling kita, yang bersama-sama menjadi sebahagian daripada sesebuah kelompok atau komuniti.
Begitulah Islam mementingkan kesejahteraan jiran tetangga. Kita dituntut berbuat baik kepada jiran walaupun berbeza warna kulit dan kepercayaan.
Tetapi watak pengacau tetap ada.
Bukan di rumah sahaja. Di dalam bilik darjah, pasti ada seorang watak pengacau atau kaki buli. Di pejabat pula ada kaki mengadu domba.
Malah, di peringkat dunia pun ada negara yang kita panggil jiran tetapi suka buat hal.
Tiap-tiap tahun rumah kita dimasuki asap gara-gara jiran membuat pembakaran “di halamannya”. Kita dan jiran-jiran lain sudah puas mengeluh, tetapi dia tidak peduli.
Apa kita hendak buat dengan mereka?
Sikap tidak mempedulikan pihak lain ini cukup membuatkan kita tertekan. Kita bingung dan mati kutu. Sampai bilakah keadaan ini akan berterusan? Bilakah pula mereka akan sedar dan berubah?
Maka, setelah puas mengeluh, ayuhlah kita berdoa kepada tuhan agar pintu akal mereka terbuka dan mereka menjadi lebih bijak sedikit.
Berdoalah sungguh-sungguh sebelum terlambat. Sebelum keamanan dan kesihatan kita musnah.
Bukan apa.
Saya sudah bosan dengan jerebu ini.
Tolonglah, wahai jiran!
Bebaskan kami daripada kekaburan yang melemaskan paru-paru ini.
Kami semakin tidak tahan!

773c6020d7b35831: From Moaz Nair
Not too long ago, Negeri Sembilan stood proud as a bastion of political tranquillity amidst a turbulent national landscape.

Under the previous Barisan Nasional–Pakatan Harapan coalition government led by former menteri besar Aminuddin Harun, the state enjoyed a rare commodity in modern Malaysian politics: absolute administrative stability.

Today, that hard-won stability has been recklessly squandered. Negeri Sembilan now finds itself ensnared in a historic, multi-layered constitutional crisis born entirely of the current government’s own missteps.

For the voters, legal experts, and everyday citizens witnessing this paralysis, the contrast between past order and present dysfunction could not be starker. The memory of the previous BN-PH framework is fast becoming the definitive benchmark for stable governance and a bitter reminder of how far the state has fallen.

The crowning achievement of the previous administration was its meticulous commitment to preserving constitutional harmony and institutional traditions. Negeri Sembilan’s governance model is uniquely complex, relying on a centuries-old, delicate equilibrium between a modern elected executive, the monarchy, and the state’s sacred, uncodified Adat Perpatih (customary law) institutions.

Aminuddin’s government managed this sensitive balance not by luck, but through sheer political maturity and institutional restraint. Recognising the vital need to insulate daily partisan politics from royal affairs, his government maintained a peaceful, respectful coexistence between elected officials, the Undang Yang Empat (traditional chieftains), and the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Mutual respect
It was a partnership built on mutual respect and systemic boundaries, ensuring that time-honoured traditions and modern democracy reinforced rather than undermined one another.

Crucially, this political maturity served as a protective shield that insulated the state from systemic crises. Backers of the previous government frequently note that the coalition successfully shielded the civil service and state apparatus from being dragged into protracted constitutional disputes.

Today, we realise just how vital that bulwark was, and how easily it could be dismantled by naked political opportunism. The moment the BN-PH cooperation fractured, it triggered an unprecedented and destructive chain reaction that has shaken the state to its core.

The descent into absolute turmoil accelerated rapidly last April, when 14 BN assemblymen abruptly withdrew their support from Aminuddin’s government following a dispute involving royal affairs. Rather than prioritising state stability, this drastic move plunged the state into a perilous political vacuum, leaving a minority government in its wake and forcing a snap election.

This vacuum did more than just disrupt daily executive governance; it threw open the doors to the current existential crisis— an unprecedented, overt succession dispute between Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, who is backed by the current administration.
Constitutional deadlock
The collapse of the foundational political consensus has dragged the state legislative assembly into a complex, multi-layered constitutional deadlock with no clear legal exit ramp.

We are now forced to witness an extraordinary and embarrassing clash of powers. In direct response to aggressive moves by the new state executive council supporting a proclamation to depose him, Tuanku Muhriz took the radical but decisive step of revoking the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors. Citing a direct breach of their oaths of office, the palace purged the state cabinet in one swift stroke.

The fallout has left governance not just shaky, but completely paralysed. The current menteri besar, Ismail Lasim, now stands isolated—a lone captain aboard a ghost ship. In a bizarre attempt to downplay this structural damage, Ismail has chosen to prioritise appointing village chiefs and village development and security committees rather than resolving the critical vacancies in his cabinet.

To claim that state administration is "running smoothly" while the formal sitting of the state assembly has been indefinitely postponed until late November is an insult to the voters' intelligence. This represents a profound failure of the democratic apparatus, where grassroots local appointments are being deployed as a smoke screen to mask a total absence of executive authority.
Painful lesson

Negeri Sembilan is learning a painful lesson first-hand: when you dismantle a functional political consensus for short-term gain, the alternative is rarely better. The current turmoil proves that the previous BN-PH ruling alliance was not merely a marriage of convenience — it was a vital stabilising force.

The current menteri besar cannot continue to govern in a state of absolute paralysis, pretending that village-level appointments can substitute for a functioning state legislative assembly or a complete Exco line-up.

The state’s political leaders must urgently put aside partisan egos, halt their dangerous chess game against traditional institutions, and return to the constitutional blueprint that guaranteed peace for years. The state's executive vacuum is no longer an isolated political squabble; it is a systemic crisis threatening the very fabric of Negeri Sembilan’s unique identity.
If the current leadership is incapable of restoring the stable, respectful equilibrium of the past, they must accept their failure and step aside for those who can.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

5896ab894451fee5: Over the Merdeka holidays, I went fishing with some friends off the Pahang and Johor coast. We started off from the Kuala Rompin jetties on a lovely morning with mist shrouding the mangrove and hovering over the river. It was a beautiful, peaceful sight.

Then the sun started getting hotter but the mist remained… and remained, acting in a most un-misty way. When we sailed away from the river mouth we could still see this “mist” all around us. It wasn’t mist. It was the haze, right there on the east coast hundreds of kilometres from the nearest Indonesian territories, yet enough of it was visible even in Pulau Tioman.

Over the last few months, I've been saying “I've never seen haze this bad, only to update it again multiple times on subsequent days. The haze last week was especially bad, but I’m sure as records go this too will be broken soon.

What can I say about the haze that hasn’t been said by many for years? I’m relatively healthy for my age and don’t have any bad allergy problems, but I still get headaches and nausea because of it. I can’t bear to think about what those with actual health issues must be going through.
The current haze seems worse than previous ones. It hangs heavy and feels thick and foul, often covering the sun and hills and gloomily blocking vision to barely a kilometre or so on the highway.

Everybody is frustrated with it, including an Indonesian official who slammed his Malaysian and Singaporean neighbours for complaining about the haze from Sumatra without acknowledging it also gives us oxygen during better days.

Hello! Our Indonesian official friend forgets his high school chemistry. Sumatra is passing us more than oxygen now, this time the said oxygen is all bound up with carbon and sulphur and nitrogen and other elements to form noxious and poisonous monoxides and dioxides and ozone!
Not exactly the kind of trade among friends. After decades of “importing” this stuff for months most years, we deserve a breather, if you’ll pardon the expression.
The Indonesians are also experimenting with clearing the haze with dry ice, which is supposed to lift the smoke particles higher into the atmosphere and clear the land.

Great – now the smoke particles will go even higher into the Indonesian skies to catch the stronger monsoon wind up there and even more of them can waft their way to Malaysia. Thank you again Indonesia!

In reality, Indonesia’s forest fire problem has gotten out of hand. The fires have literally gone underground, setting off the uncontrollable burning of dry underground peat. Once this catches fire, only the deluge of a monsoon can put it out.

This year a combination of factors, including a more severe El Nino, is exacerbating the problem; perhaps a madder-than-usual rush to burn forests, because there’s less of them left every year, is making things worse.

What we need to see is a more aggressive attitude among the political leaders of the region in fighting this menace. Our own leaders must also start demanding more be done by Indonesia to stop this perennial curse.

Of the culprits setting the forest on fire in Sumatra and Kalimantan are believed to include some big Malaysian plantation companies. If that is so, bring them to account and throw the book at them: I can guarantee there’ll be loud cheers from us ordinary Malaysians.
And ordinary Indonesians too. If it’s bad for us hundreds of kilometres away from the worst of it, just imagine how bad it must be for the unfortunate people living right there.

They can't go fishing away from the haze, like I did. They can’t get into private jets and fly out of the country to foreign clearer skies, as some people did. They just have to stay there and suck it all in literally and suffer now and/or die earlier later.

Our problems are not with the ordinary Indonesians, many of whom suffer even worse than us because of this haze. Our issues are with the Indonesian authorities who we don’t see treating the problem as the emergency it actually is.
And our issue is also with our own leaders who are more interested in maintaining peace and harmony while our people are literally choking with illness and maybe even death.

24b825d8c47931f2: Pennsylvania's health department issued a health alert Monday as cases of measles in pregnancy and, in turn, cases of congenital measles have continued to increase. Before the current outbreak—which continues to rage across the state—congenital measles cases hadn't been seen in decades, the department noted in its advisory.

The alert included detailed clinical guidance for managing measles exposures and cases during pregnancy as well as cases in newborns. Many doctors have never seen such cases in their careers given the decades of successful use of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. But now, with vaccination rates slipping nationwide, the highly infectious virus is better able to get footholds in communities and spread rapidly through under-vaccinated pockets, as is happening in Pennsylvania.

As of October 19, Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 measles cases this year across 42 counties. Of those, 247 have been hospitalized, and six people have reportedly died (though the latest reported death is still pending an investigation by the state health department before it is added to the state tally).

8b2c60ecf7a9eebf: The first order of business for the energy transition is electrifying applications like vehicles and heating and making sure that the electricity that powers them is made using renewables. But once the dominant slices of the emissions pie have shrunk, other categories with less potential to reduce emissions become important.

A new study led by Haiwei Zhou at the University of Melbourne focused on the emissions associated with making lithium-ion batteries, which many parts of the energy transition rely on. Those emissions aren’t zero, so as we use more and more batteries, that number will grow. Right now, the researchers estimate that these emissions only account for 0.18 percent of annual greenhouse gas releases, but they could increase by a factor of 10 or more by 2050.

There are a number of ways to reduce the emissions required to make a battery. Some elements used in various lithium-ion battery chemistries are more energy-intensive to mine and refine than others. The battery manufacturing process involves many steps that could be made more energy-efficient. And then there’s recycling, which can put battery materials back into the loop while requiring much less energy than mining.
6dcd14183fe24565: Recently fixed vulnerabilities in the Plex Media Server are under active exploitation in attacks that, when successful, install malware, including cryptominers and residential proxy apps, a researcher said.

Plex fixed four vulnerabilities at the start of last month. Three weeks later, published CVE designations revealed five vulnerabilities, with one of them carrying a severity rating of 8.6 out of 10. A researcher last week revealed an exploit that chained four of them together to achieve remote code execution of the device running a vulnerable Plex version. The researcher named the chain "Plex2Shell."

The new details allowed a separate researcher to create a honeypot that could track attempts in the wild to exploit the vulnerability chain. Within a day, the researcher began seeing active scanning of the simulated Plex server and eventually successful attempts to infect devices. So far, successful attacks are installing two payloads. One is a cryptominer, which uses the device to mine cryptocurrency and deposit it into a wallet controlled by the attacker. The other payload is residential proxy software, which allows people to anonymize their Internet activity (much of it illegal) by connecting to the infected box and then using it to send the user’s traffic to a final destination.
